strategy.headline: The '77 title turns 50 in Nike's hometown. Build it for the Big Dark, with Albina.
strategy.thesis: Portland is a loyal, one-team town, and a lot of the people in its stands design sportswear for a living. They reward craft and can spot a corporate template from the upper deck. In 2026-27 the Blazers have no new City Edition (they're re-wearing 2019-20), no Specter kit and no opening-night or Christmas game. But June 5, 2027 is the 50th anniversary of the city's only title, won in a Coliseum built on cleared Black Albina blocks. Nike makes every Blazers jersey, yet the franchise icon wears adidas and Morant's role and brand standing are unsettled. So sell team and city marks and the whole roster, not one athlete. The order: sign Albina co-authors and clear heritage rights this fall, and tell the '77 story now with logo-only product. Ship the licensed Blazermania 50 line from February to June 5. Stock existing storm gear for the Big Dark, and seed a 2028-29 City Edition built with Albina.

archetype.name: The Insider Loyalist
archetype.description: A fan base that stayed through 814 sellouts, the Jail Blazers and Lillard's exit and return. It lives next door to Beaverton, so it reads every jersey for fabric, fit and who designed it. It wants its story told from inside the city, never as a Portlandia punchline.

pulse.teamMoment: New owner Tom Dundon's Blazers add Ja Morant, acquired from Memphis on June 29, to a backcourt with Damian Lillard, back from a torn Achilles. Micah Nori is the first-year coach. Last season went 42-40 and ended 4-1 to San Antonio in the first round. Oregon, Multnomah County and Portland have committed $586M to Moda Center upgrades, but the lease is still unsigned.
pulse.sentiment: Hopeful but guarded. Fans are emotional about Lillard back in a Blazers uniform after a lost season, and split on Morant's talent versus his 2023 suspensions. They debate whether Nori brings one of them off the bench. They're relieved the team is staying, and wary of an owner who says he won't pay for the renovation.

topInsights.title: A heritage year with no heritage product
topInsights.insight: The 1977 title turns 50 on June 5, 2027. Portland is re-wearing its 2019-20 City Edition, sits outside Nike's eight-team Specter program and has no opening-night or Christmas game. Nothing on the league calendar marks the city's biggest story of the season.
topInsights.implication: Tell the story from October with logo-only product. Ship the licensed Blazermania 50 line from February, once alumni, estate and league rights clear: a '77 warmup and a 1977-2027 patch shooter. Pitch a 1976-77 Classic look for one night, June 5, not as a season jersey.

topInsights.title: Nike makes the jersey; adidas owns the face
topInsights.insight: Lillard's #0 is the most-worn modern Blazers jersey, but he's an adidas signature athlete, and adidas North America sits in North Portland. Morant brings two 2023 suspensions to a fan base that still winces at the Jail Blazers. Either may come off the bench. Fans are already buying Avdija and Sharpe shirts.
topInsights.implication: Build a jersey wall that survives any depth chart: Lillard, Morant, Avdija, Sharpe, Clingan and youth sizes, plus a whole-roster tee. Keep 'Dame Time' and his marks off product. Keep Avdija free of national or political symbols. Treat any Ja Portland colorway as a late bonus.

topInsights.title: The arena sits on Albina, and that land is being re-decided now
topInsights.insight: Memorial Coliseum, where the 1977 title was won, was built by clearing Lower Albina's homes, Bethel AME and Jumptown's Black businesses. In September 2026 the City Council approved development talks with Albina Vision Trust on city land next to the Moda Center. Nike's Community Store on NE MLK has long hired from the neighborhood.
topInsights.implication: Albina partners must co-author Blazermania 50, signed and paid before any heritage drop, with the displacement story on hangtags. Celebrating the Coliseum without them is exactly the nostalgia this city calls out.

topInsights.title: The fan uniform is a jersey over a hoodie under a shell
topInsights.insight: The season lives inside the Big Dark. Steady rain usually returns in mid-October, and the Nov 1 clock change pulls sunset to about 5 pm. Fans ride MAX to the Rose Quarter in drizzle, hoods up, no umbrellas. Rain, not cold, drives outerwear demand.
topInsights.implication: This season, put Nike's existing Storm-FIT and Therma-FIT team outerwear in Blazers colors on the floor from mid-October, and market around Nov 1. Make the bespoke Big Dark shell the FW27 hero, long enough to cover a Swingman.

topInsights.title: The most Nike-literate crowd anywhere punishes fake heritage
topInsights.insight: Samples, employee-store finds and 1990s Blazers warmups turn up at the Bins and on Hawthorne's vintage racks, where pickers date gear by its tag. Mitchell & Ness already sells Walton-era replicas. The record-store and gig-poster scene rewards numbered, hand-pulled short runs.
topInsights.implication: Make heritage pieces archive-exact or clearly new, never a near-copy of a replica fans already own. Keep Portland exclusives scarce and raffle them locally, with a credited 'designed in Rip City' story.

topInsights.title: Local makers beat the team to the moment
topInsights.insight: When the team said there would be no 2026 playoff shirts, Portland Gear and Hyder Graphics printed 200 'Red Hot Rising' tees in about 48 hours. Troy Douglass hoisted the old Blazers on Broadway ball over his Hawthorne shop before the first home playoff game.
topInsights.implication: License that speed instead of taming it. Agree NBA terms with Portland Gear in winter, with creative control and a fast written approval path. Stage red blanks so the next clinch gets official, artist-credited product within 48 hours.

topInsights.title: Rip City has two audiences outside the core
topInsights.insight: Rip City's map crosses the Columbia to tax-free shopping in SW Washington. It runs down the valley to Woodburn, Eugene and Bend, where fans wear Blazers gear alongside Ducks or Beavers gear. Summer belongs to Providence Park's women's-sports supporters and the WNBA's Portland Fire at the Moda Center.
topInsights.implication: Test any '541' or statewide idea with Eugene and Bend fans before it ships. Open Woodburn as a Spanish-language, community-led door. Make summer Rip City product women's-first and supporter-made, with Fire marks only under license.

collection.name: Rip City, All Right
collection.story: Named for Bill Schonely's first-season call. Portland has been designing sport since the 1970 pinwheel and the 1971 Swoosh, and this collection treats it that way. It runs from the 1977 Glass Palace to the Big Dark walk from the MAX, and from Albina's courts to a women's-first summer. Every graphic comes from the city's own vocabulary, and every community cue is co-authored and paid.

uniform.narrative: The Blazers were born and won it all in Memorial Coliseum, a glowing glass box built on Lower Albina blocks cleared of Black homes, Bethel AME and Jumptown's clubs. A City Edition started now realistically debuts in 2028-29. It tells both stories, with or without renovation news: the building where Blazermania began and the neighborhood under it. Black Portland partners get a real say in decisions. After four seasons of carpet and plaid and a 2019-20 re-wear, this is the uniform locals haven't seen.
motifs: Coliseum curtain-wall grid as a tonal jacquard across the body
Original artwork by commissioned Albina artists on the side panels, in dialogue with (never copying) the Black Williams tiles
Five-and-five pinwheel stripes as collar and armhole trim
A small sunbreak-gold glow line along the grid, as the Coliseum reads at night
uniform.typography: A 'PORTLAND' wordmark in an original alphabet by a Black Portland letterer, drawn from the Jumptown-era marquee tradition. Cream block numbers outlined in red. No pioneer or wagon type.
details: Jock tag and inside neck tape crediting the co-designing artists and partners, subject to NBA rules on City Edition tag content and the partners' sign-off on wording
A written proceeds commitment to an Albina organization the partners choose, agreed before any announcement
Optional court tie-in (grid-pattern baseline art) only if the renovation proceeds and its local-art program confirms
Launch at the Nike Community Store on NE MLK, announced only after the Moda Center lease is signed
avoid: A fifth plaid or PDX carpet story; keep them to linings at most
Nostalgic jazz-age or Coliseum imagery that skips the displacement, or any version Albina partners have not approved

Oregon Trail, pioneer or generic 'PNW tribal' imagery. Any Native element goes only through an Oregon nation (Grand Ronde, Siletz, Warm Springs) and a named Oregon artist paid up front, with tribal approval or veto
Lillard's personal marks, Grateful Dead imagery, the Portlandia statue or other third-party IP
Tying the story to the new ownership or a 'new era' before the lease is signed

partners.why: D'Wayne Edwards's school and its Sneaker Week feed young Portland designers straight into the industry: the 'designed in Rip City' story, for real.
partners.idea: A paid student brief for the 2027 holiday neon-lettering drop, with credited finalists and an Old Town launch.

partners.name: Self Enhancement, Inc. (SEI)
partners.why: A long-standing Albina institution and the right paid partner for events built with Black Portland families.
partners.idea: Co-run the Matt Dishman clinics and the Irving Park summer run, with youth product and proceeds going to SEI programs.

Rip City Clothing Co. at Moda Center for jersey volume. Push for a street-facing team store in the renovation once the lease is signed
Old Town Chinatown (Compound Gallery, Deadstock Coffee at The Hoxton, Pensole) to set taste before the malls. Nike Portland downtown only if it will carry Blazers product
Woodburn, Jantzen Beach and Washington Square for the SW Washington, Latino and suburban family shoppers
Portland Gear for clinch-speed releases under a pre-agreed license

Lillard's confirmed return through the Oct 30 Cup night for jerseys, chased weekly
Black Friday to Dec 24 for gifting, marketed to ship-by dates
February to June 5 for licensed heritage drops, after partners and rights are signed
April clinch windows within 48 hours, staged but not pre-produced
how: Partners first, rights next, product third. No heritage or Albina product until co-authors are signed and paid
Lead with team and city marks and a whole-roster wall. Keep Lillard's personal marks off product, and treat Ja product as a bonus once cleared
Make exclusives scarce and archive-exact, released by local raffle rather than in lines resellers dominate
Credit and pay every local artist, printer and community partner by name on tags and in launch content
Cut fan product to layer: jerseys over hoodies, shells long enough to cover a Swingman

risks.risk: Lead times. It's October, fall product is locked, and 1977 likeness, estate, league and patch approvals take months.
risks.mitigation: Ship only logo-only and existing product this fall. Make February-March the first licensed heritage drop, and keep the June 5 finale to 3 or 4 styles. Move bespoke Big Dark outerwear to FW27.

risks.risk: Using Albina, Vanport and Coliseum stories as backdrop, or launching before partners sign, would look like a hometown giant selling Black Portland's displacement. AVT may also decline a tie while it negotiates land with the city.
risks.mitigation: Ask AVT first, with veto and an open exit, and keep a Plan B led by Oregon Black Pioneers. Sign and pay co-authors before Drop 1. Put proceeds commitments in writing before announcing.

risks.risk: Lillard is an adidas athlete. Morant's 2023 suspensions sit uneasily with a fan base shaped by the Jail Blazers. Either may come off the bench or miss time.
risks.mitigation: Keep Lillard to NBA-licensed jerseys and team marks, and stock a whole-roster wall chased weekly. Run a brand-safety review before any Morant-led product, with a plan to pause it.

risks.risk: The unsigned Moda Center lease, and an owner who says he won't pay for the renovation, could stall arena retail or turn fans against 'new era' messaging.
risks.mitigation: Build the City Edition to stand without renovation news and keep court tie-ins optional. Announce nothing until the lease is signed. Keep 'Moda Center' off long-life product.

risks.risk: Third-party IP is everywhere: the PDX carpet, Pendleton plaids, Grateful Dead marks, KPM's 'The Trumpets', 1977 likenesses, Mitchell & Ness replicas, Fire, Thorns, college and school marks.
risks.mitigation: Clear licenses and estate permissions before design lock. Recreate ideas rather than reproduce artwork, and keep plaid and carpet to linings. Frame summer pieces as supporter-made Blazers product until a Fire license exists.

scorecard.rationale: Nike's hometown, a once-only '77-at-50 year, a Lillard-Morant backcourt and intense statewide loyalty lift opportunity and fandom well above average, while few public Nike doors and a Rose Quarter retail desert put retail below it (brief scores: opportunity 76, culture 84, retail 56, fandom 80). A once-only heritage year, an empty City Edition slot and a deep roster in Nike's own hometown make the opportunity large. Albina, Rip City broadcast lore, maker craft and supporter culture give unusually deep design material. Retail lags: the metro has few public Nike doors, a thinned downtown and a Rose Quarter retail desert, and this season's lead times limit what ships before February. Fandom is intense and statewide, but guarded about Morant and the owner.

music.headline: Portland's music grew up in Albina's clubs and on its telephone poles.
music.summary: Portland music runs on two engines: the Black Albina tradition, from 1940s 'Jumptown' jazz to 1970s funk, and a DIY scene that still papers telephone poles with screenprinted gig posters. The Blazers plug into both through DJ O.G. ONE and 'The Trumpets.' The team's two biggest music names, Lillard and Aminé, wear rival brands. So Nike's lane is the scene itself: its institutions, non-conflicted rappers and print artists, timed to Albina's summer festivals.

insights.title: The arena sits on Jumptown's footprint
insights.detail: Albina's Williams Avenue clubs (the Dude Ranch, the Savoy, Jackie's) earned the 1940s-50s nickname 'Jumptown.' Building Memorial Coliseum, the Blazers' first home, demolished 476 housing units, Bethel AME Church and Black-owned businesses in Lower Albina. In September 2026 City Council approved talks with Black-led Albina Vision Trust on about 6.2 acres of city land around the Moda Center.
insights.implication: Portland's richest music story is also the arena's original wound. Tell it only as a paid, co-authored partnership with Albina Music Trust and Albina Vision Trust, ideally with proceeds tied to the Lower Albina rebuild. Never use nostalgic jazz-age graphics.

insights.title: DJ O.G. ONE is the bridge between the team and local hip-hop
insights.detail: David Jackson has spun Blazers home games for well over a decade. He co-founded PDX Hip Hop Week, which started after a 2013 wave of shutdowns of clubs serving hip-hop and Black and brown crowds. He also hosted Wynne's 2025 mixtape 'Say Wynne,' which features Dame D.O.L.L.A. The city has proclaimed Nov. 30 'DJ O.G. ONE Day.'
insights.implication: Make him the paid music curator for any Blazers city collection. He can vouch for local artists, soundtrack launch content and host drops with credibility no brand team can buy.

insights.title: The team's sonic logo is a 1976 brass fanfare
insights.detail: 'The Trumpets' is officially Brian Bennett's 'Capital City,' from KPM's 1976 library album 'Hot Wax.' It opened and closed Blazers broadcasts for more than 30 years. Portland band Portugal. The Man jammed it on Coachella's main stage in 2018, and the team later issued a recorded version.
insights.implication: Only Blazers fans decode the brass fanfare, so use it as a heritage cue: horn-bell graphics, brass hardware, a 'Trumpets' warmup. Any audio on product or in content needs a KPM license.

insights.title: Analog, small-batch, pole-postered
insights.detail: Music Millennium (East Burnside, open since 1969, the Northwest's oldest record store) is now seeking a successor owner. Mississippi Records on N Albina Ave and Speck's in Kenton anchor the vinyl culture too. Mike King's screenprinted gig posters grew out of Portland punk flyering. Dead Moon pressed records on the lathe that cut 'Louie Louie.'
insights.implication: Drop city product like a record: numbered short runs, screenprinted graphics, poster inserts, pickup at record stores and venues. Locals reward craft and scarcity over mass hype.

insights.title: The two loudest local voices are signed elsewhere
insights.detail: Lillard (Dame D.O.L.L.A.) returns Oct 21 against Phoenix, but he's an adidas signature athlete. Aminé, raised in Woodlawn, has a Rip City tattoo and filled his 'Woodlawn' video with Blazers merch. He is also releasing a New Balance 992 'Outdoor School' this month. Wynne raps about Nike, features Dame and toured Portland's small rooms in September 2025.
insights.implication: Celebrate Lillard only through NBA-licensed jersey and team-store product. Build artist collabs with non-conflicted locals such as Wynne, Cool Nutz and the Soul Assembly producers.

insights.title: Albina's music season is the Blazers' off-season
insights.detail: Juneteenth Oregon (54th year, June 20, 2026) parades up MLK Jr. Blvd to Lillis Albina Park. A week later the park hosts Good in the Hood, with a POH-Hop set from Cool Nutz. PDX Hip Hop Week then runs Aug. 20-26 and ends with a skate night at Oaks Park's 1906 rink.
insights.implication: Use the June-August festival stages, a few blocks from the arena, to co-create and preview next season's city product with local artists. Launch it at the October home opener.

insights.title: Tie-dye is earned Blazers heritage
insights.detail: Bill Walton, MVP of the 1977 Finals, was a Deadhead with more than 1,000 shows. In 2024-25 the Blazers wore a tie-dye Walton band and held a tribute night with the Garcia Birthday Band at halftime. They also sold a Grateful Dead x Blazers tie-dye shirt with a group-ticket package.
insights.implication: Here tie-dye reads as Rip City history, not hippie cliché. Use it as a lining, band or one-night tribute capsule. Grateful Dead marks need a license. Follow the team's precedent on proceeds: the Maurice Lucas Foundation.

places.name: Lillis Albina Park
places.why: Hosts Juneteenth Oregon and Good in the Hood, a few blocks north of the Rose Quarter, in the community the arena district displaced.

places.name: Wonder Ballroom
places.why: A 1914 hall on Russell Street, once the commercial spine of Black Albina, and the right size for a city-product launch show.

places.name: Jefferson High School
places.why: Home of the 1968 'Soul Assembly' and the soul scene that fed funk band Pleasure. The Jefferson Dancers marked 50 years in 2026.

places.name: McMenamins Crystal Ballroom
places.why: A 1914 ballroom with a floating dance floor. Lillard sold out his first Dame D.O.L.L.A. concert here on his 26th birthday in 2016.

places.name: The Get Down
places.neighborhood: Central Eastside (SE 6th Ave, beneath Melody Ballroom)
places.why: A neon-lit basement club, open since 2022, for funk, cumbia and beat-driven dance nights. It's the current home of the city's after-dark groove crowd.

places.name: Alberta Street Pub
places.why: Hosts the PDX Hip Hop Week kickoff after-party and was a stop on Wynne's 2025 'Tour Next Door.' It's where the local rap community actually hangs out.

places.name: Oaks Park Roller Skating Rink
places.why: A 1906 rink that still skates to a live 1926 Wurlitzer pipe organ. It hosts the PDX Hip Hop Week skate party with DJ O.G. ONE.

places.name: Speck's Records & Tapes
places.why: A North Portland shop where Wynne launched her 2025 hometown tour. It's the NoPo crate-digger's stop.

places.name: Mississippi Records
places.why: A cult shop and label (reissues of Dead Moon and Ural Thomas) whose handmade collage sleeves define Portland's lo-fi look.

places.name: Music Millennium
places.why: The Northwest's oldest record store (1969), with an in-store stage. Owner Terry Currier began searching for a successor in 2026.

people.name: DJ O.G. ONE (David Jackson)
people.role: Trail Blazers in-arena DJ; co-founder of PDX Hip Hop Week
people.why: The most credible connector between the team and local music. The city honors him each Nov. 30.

people.name: Aminé
people.role: Rapper raised in NE Portland's Woodlawn; Benson Polytechnic alum
people.why: Portland's biggest music export and an outspoken Blazers fan, but a New Balance partner. Admire him without co-opting him.

people.name: Dame D.O.L.L.A. (Damian Lillard)
people.role: Blazers guard, franchise scoring leader and rapper
people.why: Back on the floor Oct 21, 2026, he is the team's music face. As an adidas signature athlete, he's usable only through licensed NBA product.

people.name: Wynne
people.role: Lake Oswego-raised Portland rapper
people.why: She name-checks Nike, has recorded with Dame and wrote UO women's hoops anthem 'Throw the O.' She's the most natural local collab voice.

people.name: Cool Nutz (Terrance Scott)
people.role: Rapper; co-founder of Jus Family Records (1992) and founder of the POH-Hop festival (1995)
people.why: The elder statesman of Portland rap and an Oregon Music Hall of Fame honoree, still headlining Albina's festivals.

people.name: Albina Music Trust
people.role: Archive and label for Albina's 1960s-80s Black music (founded by Bobby Smith with the World Arts Foundation)
people.why: Holds the recordings, photos and stories behind any Albina music product. Its 2025 'Soul Assembly' remix LP made the Portland Mercury's top-10 local albums.

people.name: Pleasure
people.role: 1970s Portland funk band (Fantasy Records; 'Glide')
people.why: Grew out of Jefferson High's soul scene and has been back onstage since 2019. A living link between Albina's history and today's stages.

people.name: Mike King
people.role: Gig-poster artist who came up in Portland punk
people.why: Called America's most prolific gig-poster artist, and the subject of a 2026 five-decade retrospective. The obvious commission for a Blazers poster series.

moments.name: Home opener and Lillard's return
moments.why: Lillard's first regular-season Blazers game since 2023 and Ja Morant's debut make this the loudest arena night of the year for a music-led drop.

moments.name: DJ O.G. ONE Day
moments.why: The city honors the Blazers DJ with a proclaimed day. It fits a local-music game night early in the season.

moments.name: Biamp Portland Jazz Festival (PDX Jazz)
moments.why: Over 50 shows in about 30 venues. Portland's jazz festival, historically tied to Black History Month, now lands during the playoff push.

moments.name: Juneteenth Oregon Parade & Festival
moments.why: In its 54th year, the Clara Peoples Freedom Trail Parade travels MLK Jr. Blvd to Lillis Albina Park, with Albina soul veterans like Calvin Walker on stage.

moments.name: Good in the Hood
moments.why: Portland's longest-running multicultural music and food festival, rooted in Albina. The 2026 bill included POH-Hop with Cool Nutz.

moments.name: Waterfront Blues Festival
moments.why: The biggest music weekend on the downtown riverfront ends in fireworks. It's peak summer reach for city product.

moments.name: Cathedral Park Jazz Festival
moments.why: A free jazz festival under the St. Johns Bridge in NoPo, now 46 years running. Neighborhood-scale and local to the bone.

moments.name: PDX Hip Hop Week and STAR Awards
moments.why: Honoring late co-founder Star Chile, the week runs from a City Hall block party to Oaks Park skate night. It's the pre-season window to seed product with the hip-hop community.

Nickname for Albina's 1940s-50s Williams Avenue jazz and blues club strip.
Fans' name for the Blazers' brass broadcast theme, Brian Bennett's library track 'Capital City.'
The Jefferson High Black Student Union's 1968 cultural program. Now the name of Albina Music Trust's remix series.
The Portland Oregon Hip-Hop Festival. Cool Nutz started it in 1995 after clubs refused to book rap.
North Portland (St. Johns, Kenton, Arbor Lodge), home turf for much of the city's rap and crate-digging.

designCues.cue: Day-Glo copier pink on Portland gray
designCues.source: Fluorescent flyers stapled to wooden telephone poles, built to pop under overcast skies. This is the gig-poster culture Mike King came out of.
designCues.use: Use as a single hit color (taping, hangtag, inside placket) against black and Blazers red. The hex approximates fluorescent stock, so match it with a neon lab dip.

designCues.cue: Remix Natural: an unbleached-cream base from the 1970s palette
designCues.source: The Rip City Remix palette (Remix Black, Red, Natural, Maroon, White), built to echo the franchise's 1970s founding era.
designCues.use: Use as an ecru or natural cotton base for a heritage-music capsule. The hex is approximate, so pull the official value from the Blazers' brand guide.

designCues.cue: The pinwheel as vinyl: the Blazers' five-and-five stripes flattened into a record
designCues.source: The Rip City Remix logo, which redrew the team pinwheel to read as a vinyl record.
designCues.use: Apply as a concentric groove emboss on shooting shirts, a record-label center patch, or hangtags shaped like 7-inch sleeves. It's in-house team IP.

designCues.cue: Brass fanfare: trumpet bells and horn lines
designCues.source: 'The Trumpets,' the Blazers' broadcast theme for more than 30 years.
designCues.use: Use horn-bell line art on warmups and brass-tone zipper pulls or aglets. Don't pair it with the actual audio without a KPM license.

designCues.cue: Hand-lettered liner-note type and cut-and-paste collage
designCues.source: Mississippi Records' handwritten, collaged sleeves and Fred Cole's homemade Dead Moon art.
designCues.use: Commission Portland letterers and collage artists for inside-collar 'liner notes' and hangtags. Don't imitate any one label's house style.

designCues.cue: Two- or three-color screenprint with slight misregistration
designCues.source: The Portland gig-poster lineage of hand-pulled, limited-color screenprints.
designCues.use: Use water-based prints that look hand-pulled, from original commissioned art. Credit the artist on the tag.

designCues.cue: Walton tie-dye spiral
designCues.source: Bill Walton's Deadhead identity, honored with a tie-dye jersey band in 2024-25.
designCues.use: Use as a lining, waistband or headband accent for an annual tribute night. Leave out Grateful Dead marks (dancing bears, Steal Your Face) unless licensed.

designCues.cue: Soul Assembly, from 1968 to now
designCues.source: The Jefferson High Black Student Union's 1968 response to Dr. King's assassination, revived in Albina Music Trust's 2025 remix LP of Albina recordings.
designCues.use: Make it the story anchor for a Juneteenth or Black History capsule built on licensed Albina Music Trust photography. Give credit, pay fees and share revenue.

productHooks: A 'Trumpets' pregame shooting shirt with horn-bell graphics, a vinyl-groove pinwheel emboss and a Remix-cream base. Release it for the Oct 21 Lillard-return opener, with a DJ O.G. ONE Portland mix as launch content (audio licensed).

A PDX Hip Hop Week capsule (Aug. 20-26), co-designed with DJ O.G. ONE and STAR Awards honorees. Sell it at the City Hall block party and the Oaks Park skate night, with proceeds to the week's youth programming.

A 'Soul Assembly' Albina capsule using licensed Albina Music Trust archive photos and track-title graphics. Preview it at Juneteenth Oregon and Good in the Hood in Lillis Albina Park, with a revenue share to the Trust.

A record-store run of numbered screenprinted tees, each with a commissioned Portland game poster inside. Sell only through Music Millennium, Mississippi Records and Speck's around Record Store Day in April, as the playoff push peaks.
A Walton tie-dye tribute pack (headband, crew socks, tie-dye-lined shorts) for an annual Walton night, with proceeds to the Maurice Lucas Foundation as in 2025.
A non-conflicted local-artist collab, such as Wynne writing a Rip City lyric printed on a hoodie sleeve, debuted at a Wonder Ballroom show.
watchouts: Brand conflicts: Damian Lillard is an adidas signature athlete (Dame X). Aminé is a New Balance partner (992 'Outdoor School,' October 2026). Use Lillard only through NBA-licensed player assets. Never imply Aminé endorses anything. Keep 'Dame Time' off product without his sign-off.

Albina's music history is a history of displacement. Memorial Coliseum alone erased 476 homes, Bethel AME and Black businesses. Any Jumptown or Soul Assembly product must be co-created with, credited to and paid to Black Portland institutions (Albina Music Trust, World Arts Foundation, Albina Vision Trust).
Third-party IP: 'The Trumpets' is KPM library music ('Capital City'). Grateful Dead imagery, Mississippi Records and Dead Moon artwork, and any Mike King poster all need licenses or commissions.

Currency: Doug Fir Lounge stays closed until its move to SE Morrison is finished, Music Millennium is changing owners, and PDX Jazz moved from February to March. Reconfirm venues and dates before booking.
Wynne's Nike lyrics and her Ducks anthem are not endorsements. Clear lyrics and likeness first, and keep UO's 'O' out of Blazers product.

art.headline: Portland's best design is on its bridges and signs, not its City Editions.
art.summary: Portland's look comes from civic infrastructure and handmade signs, and its murals hide from the rain under bridges. The deepest lineage is Black Albina, painted on the ground the Coliseum cleared. Local makers already move faster than the team, while City Editions keep recycling plaid and carpet. A roughly $600M Moda Center renovation has local art on its list. Commission from this bench now.

insights.title: Plaid and carpet are tapped out
insights.detail: The PDX carpet carried the 2022-23 City Edition and returned as the 2025-26 encore (19 games). In between, 2023-24 used Dr. Jack plaid, and 2024-25 wrapped the whole uniform in plaid with Mt. Hood coordinates. That's four straight seasons on two motifs.
insights.implication: Draw the next City Edition and any Portland capsule from unused local vernacular: bridge green, Old Town neon, Benson Bubbler bronze, Albina's Black Broadway, fir grain. Keep plaid and carpet as heritage accents only.

insights.title: Portland paints where the rain can't reach
insights.detail: Isaka Shamsud-Din's 1978 Albina murals rotted in the rain, and the artists took them down in 1983. Today PSAA's 'Avenue of Murals' puts 20-plus painted columns under the Hawthorne Bridge viaduct on SE Madison. They echo night watchman Tom Stefopoulos's 1948-52 Lovejoy Columns.
insights.implication: The column, a vertical wraparound canvas, is the city's native mural format. Translate it into side-panel and shorts wraps commissioned from the column muralists. The weather-tested craft story fits Nike's rain-ready outerwear.

insights.title: Black Albina is the most underused design source
insights.detail: Cleo Davis and Kayin Talton Davis's 2017 sidewalk tiles mark N Williams as Albina's 'Black Broadway.' KSMoCA runs a contemporary art museum inside Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. School. Arvie Smith, Jeremy Okai Davis and Intisar Abioto have built bodies of work on Black Portland and Black history.
insights.implication: Anchor the Blazers' February Celebration of Black History product in commissioned, paid and credited Albina artists. Skip generic Black History Month graphics.

insights.title: Old Town Chinatown is both sneaker corridor and neon district
insights.detail: Pensole's footwear school (founder of Sneaker Week) and ex-Nike developer Ian Williams's Deadstock Coffee, now inside The Hoxton, sit a few blocks from two signs. One is the restored Hung Far Low sign. The other is the White Stag 'Portland Oregon' sign, whose red neon Rudolph nose has lit up every holiday season since 1959.
insights.implication: Neon-tube lettering and the red nose give Portland a holiday story that isn't plaid. Launch it in Old Town with the sneaker community, not at a mall.

insights.title: Local makers move faster than the team
insights.detail: Blazers president Dewayne Hankins said there would be no 2026 playoff shirts. In about 48 hours, Portland Gear and Hyder Graphics printed 200 'Red Hot Rising' tees and gave them to ticket-holders. Grand Ronde tribal member Troy Douglass craned the 200-lb Blazers on Broadway steel ball onto Back to the Basket before the first home playoff game in April 2026.
insights.implication: Build a pre-cleared local-artist rapid-response program. Clinch and playoff moments then become official, artist-credited product, not a gap local brands fill.

insights.title: Indigenous design done right already has a Blazers precedent
insights.detail: At the Blazers' first Native American Heritage Month celebration (Nov 19, 2023), Coquille, Coos and Umpqua carver Shirod Younker reworked a basket design into the letters 'Rip City'. It sat on a red blanket made with Native-owned Eighth Generation.
insights.implication: Use that model for any Native-themed product: a named Oregon tribal artist, a Native-owned maker partner and a tribe-specific motif used with permission. Never use generic 'PNW tribal' pattern.

insights.title: The arena's next look is being decided now
insights.detail: Moda Center sits on Lower Albina land razed for Memorial Coliseum. In 2026 governments pledged roughly $586M toward a renovation targeted for the 2030 Women's Final Four. The city's June survey listed 'local arts and cultural elements' among nine priorities. The council is moving to make Albina Vision Trust the developer of city land across N Ramsey Way.
insights.implication: Line up City Edition, court and fan-apparel design with the renovation's local-art program from 2026 to 2030. Make Black Albina partners co-authors.

places.name: Avenue of Murals (Viaduct Arts columns)
places.neighborhood: Central Eastside (SE Madison St under the Hawthorne Bridge viaduct)
places.why: PSAA's 20-plus column murals by Hayden Senter, Jeremy Nichols, Kyra Watkins and Paola De La Cruz make the city's most current mural corridor.

places.name: Historic Black Williams Project tiles
places.why: Sidewalk tiles by Cleo Davis and Kayin Talton Davis tell the story of Albina's 'Black Broadway' block by block.

places.name: KSMoCA (Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. School Museum of Contemporary Art)
places.why: Founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, it pairs NE Portland elementary students with working artists. A ready partner for youth-led design.

places.name: White Stag 'Portland Oregon' sign
places.neighborhood: Old Town Chinatown (west end of the Burnside Bridge)
places.why: The city-owned 1940 Ramsay Signs landmark with the leaping stag is Portland's most recognizable commercial lettering.

places.name: Lovejoy Columns
places.neighborhood: Pearl District (NW 10th Ave between Everett and Flanders)
places.why: Two salvaged viaduct columns painted 1948-52 by Greek immigrant rail watchman Tom Stefopoulos. The origin story of Portland's column murals.

places.name: Pensole
places.why: D'Wayne Edwards's school runs Sneaker Week and is the most direct pipeline of young Portland footwear and product designers.

places.name: Back to the Basket
places.neighborhood: Hawthorne, SE Portland (3405 SE Hawthorne Blvd)
places.why: Troy Douglass's shop now flies the rescued Blazers on Broadway steel ball. It's the city's living archive of Blazers material culture.

places.name: Portland Art Museum and Mark Rothko Pavilion
places.why: Reopened Nov 20, 2025 after a $116M expansion, with a glass pavilion named for Rothko, who grew up in Portland and had his first solo show here.

places.name: Oregon Contemporary
places.why: The former Disjecta runs the Artists' Biennial. Emerging North Portland artists get institutional shows here.

places.name: Elizabeth Leach Gallery
places.why: Represents Jeremy Okai Davis and anchors First Thursday. The route to commissioning Portland's established painters.

people.name: Kyra Watkins
people.role: Muralist and portrait painter
people.why: Painted the 2023 Clyde Best mural at Providence Park and Avenue of Murals columns, and is a 2026 Portland Open Studios artist. She has already done sports portraiture at a Portland team's home.

people.name: Hayden Senter
people.role: Muralist
people.why: Painted the first four viaduct columns in 2023, honoring the Lovejoy Columns, Rose Festival dragon boats and the Ground Score waste pickers. Fluent in Portland's civic iconography.

people.name: Jeremy Okai Davis
people.role: Portrait painter and graphic designer (Elizabeth Leach Gallery)
people.why: Paints overlooked Black historical figures, athletes among them, in a pixelated, pointillist style. A Blazers fan and a natural Black History night collaborator.

people.name: Arvie Smith
people.role: Painter; PNCA professor emeritus; Guggenheim Fellow
people.why: The elder statesman of Black Portland painting, with murals in North Portland. A tribute or commission carries real weight in Albina.

people.name: Intisar Abioto
people.role: Photographer and artist ('The Black Portlanders')
people.why: Her intimate portraits of Black Portland are the community's own image archive, and a credible lens for campaign and product stories.

people.name: Shirod Younker
people.role: Coquille, Coos and Umpqua carver and designer
people.why: Designed the 2023 'Rip City' basket-pattern blanket with Eighth Generation. The proven template for Native collaboration with the Blazers.

people.name: Portland Gear (Marcus Harvey)
people.role: Portland streetwear brand, flagship at 403 SW 10th Ave
people.why: Founded on Black Friday 2014 as the city's unofficial outfitter, it has collaborated with the Blazers and made the 2026 'Red Hot Rising' playoff tees.

people.name: Aaron Draplin (Draplin Design Co.)
people.role: Graphic designer
people.why: Portland's best-known graphic designer and a past Nike client. His thick-line badge, patch and logo style is a local design dialect.

moments.name: First Thursday in the Pearl
moments.timing: First Thursday of every month, 5 p.m. (next: Nov 5 and Dec 3, 2026)
moments.why: The Pearl's gallery walk has run since 1986, with 150-plus artists on NW 13th. It's the standing monthly stage for artist reveals and small-run drops.

moments.name: Portland Open Studios
moments.why: About 100 metro artists open their studios in the season's opening weeks. The most efficient way to scout and sign collaborators.

moments.name: White Stag red nose lights up
moments.why: A tradition since 1959 that tells Portland the holidays have started. A ready-made launch date for a holiday capsule.

moments.name: Crafty Wonderland Holiday Art + Craft Market
moments.why: Portland's big maker market, a few blocks from Moda Center, where local illustrators and printmakers sell to the same holiday shoppers.

moments.name: Trail Blazers Celebration of Black History
moments.why: The team's established night for local Black designers' product, after the Bleached by Josh 'Rip City Made' collection.

moments.name: Portland Winter Light Festival
moments.why: Light art at Pioneer Courthouse Square and the Central Eastside's Electric Blocks. The natural stage for neon and glow-ink product.

moments.name: Vanport Mosaic Festival
moments.why: Memory-activism programming, based at the Historic Alberta House, marks the 1948 Memorial Day flood that wiped out Vanport. It's Black Portland's own frame for history-based design.

moments.name: Sneaker Week PDX
moments.why: Pensole's showcase of local artists' custom sneakers and footwear careers. Nike's home-turf talent scout.

vocabulary.meaning: Broadcaster Bill Schonely's 1971 call. Now civic shorthand for the Blazers, and the name on the team shop, Rip City Clothing.
Nickname for Portland's many river bridges and a go-to local merch word. Its signature color is the patina 'ODOT green' of the St. Johns.

vocabulary.term: Sextants (N / NE / NW / SE / SW / S)
vocabulary.meaning: Portland's address zones, called quadrants until South Portland (S) became the sixth in 2020. Residents identify with them.
The four-bowl bronze drinking fountains Simon Benson funded in 1912, designed by A.E. Doyle and still running downtown.
Plaid named for 1977 title coach Jack Ramsay's loud sport coats, used on the 2023-24 City Edition.
The teal 1987 SRG Partnership airport carpet showing the runways at night. Replaced at PDX, it lives on as merch and twice as a City Edition.
N Williams Avenue in its jazz-club heyday as the center of Black Portland, now marked by the Black Williams Project tiles.
The Blazers logo by Frank Glickman (founder Harry Glickman's cousin), 1970. Ten stripes for five players on each side meet at center court.

designCues.cue: ODOT 'bridge green': the patina green of the St. Johns Bridge and bridges statewide, spec'd as Federal Standard 595 color 24272 (on-screen approx. #3A6B4F). Match to the FS chip.
designCues.source: David Steinman picked green for the 1931 St. Johns Bridge to echo the evergreen hills. It's now painted in the ODOT green used across Oregon.
designCues.use: A base or trim color with Blazers black and red. It reads 'Bridgetown' to locals without repeating plaid or carpet teal.

designCues.cue: Stag-nose neon: Blazers red #E03A3E drawn as a glowing neon tube with a soft halo on black.
designCues.source: The White Stag sign's red Rudolph nose, lit the day before Thanksgiving every year since 1959.
designCues.use: Holiday graphics, glow and reflective inks and tonal tube lettering that suggest the nose and the neon glow. Don't copy the city-owned sign.

designCues.cue: Douglas-fir glulam amber (approx. #C4875A) with the repeating lattice rhythm of the PDX terminal roof.
designCues.source: PDX's main terminal (opened Aug 2024, designed by ZGF) is roofed with 3.5 million board feet of Douglas fir from within 300 miles.
designCues.use: A warm neutral for lifestyle fleece, trims and packaging. The lattice can become a jacquard or knit grid, credited to the architecture.

designCues.cue: Column wrap: one continuous vertical story wrapping 360 degrees around a cylinder.
designCues.source: The Avenue of Murals viaduct columns on SE Madison, descended from the 1948-52 Lovejoy Columns.
designCues.use: A painted wraparound strip on jersey side panels and shorts, commissioned from the column muralists and credited on the jock tag.

designCues.cue: Blade-sign lettering: vertically stacked capitals in outlined neon-tube strokes.
designCues.source: Old Town Chinatown's vertical signs, including the restored Hung Far Low sign at NW 4th and Couch, and the stacked 'PORTLAND OREGON' of the White Stag sign.
designCues.use: Run 'RIP CITY' or 'PORTLAND' down a side seam, hood or sleeve. Have a local sign painter draw an original alphabet rather than tracing any one sign.

designCues.cue: Cast-bronze, four-bowl Benson Bubbler details.
designCues.source: A.E. Doyle's 1912 bronze fountains, a downtown fixture for more than a century.
designCues.use: Bronze-tone metal aglets, zipper pulls and jock-tag plates, plus a four-lobed icon as a hidden Portland detail.

designCues.cue: Sextant codes: N, NE, NW, SE, SW and S as bold two-letter tags.
designCues.source: Every Portland address carries one. The Nike and Blazers court revitalization repainted park backboards with each park's quadrant.
designCues.use: Neighborhood capsules or number-style tags (NE for Albina, SE for Hawthorne) that only Portlanders decode, tied to Nike's own court work.

designCues.cue: Black Broadway tilework: the story of N Williams Avenue told in sidewalk tiles.
designCues.source: The 2017 Historic Black Williams Project tiles by Cleo Davis and Kayin Talton Davis, built from community members' memories.
designCues.use: A story and graphic language for Celebration of Black History product. Commission Albina artists to make new work in dialogue with the tiles. Never reproduce the tiles.

productHooks: 'Bridgetown' City Edition concept: an ODOT-green base, a vertical blade-sign 'RIP CITY,' a column-wrap side panel painted by a PSAA muralist and a bronze-tone jock tag with a Bubbler icon. A clear break from four seasons of plaid and carpet.

Celebration of Black History capsule (February), commissioned from an Albina artist such as Jeremy Okai Davis or Intisar Abioto. Build it around Black Portland basketball and Black Broadway figures, with proceeds to an Albina organization the artist chooses.
'Red Nose' holiday drop, released the day before Thanksgiving: black fleece with neon-red tube lettering and reflective glow. Launch it in Old Town Chinatown with Pensole and Deadstock Coffee.

48-hour clinch kit: pre-approved local-artist graphics, blanks staged with a Portland screen printer, and release through Portland Gear and Back to the Basket the moment the Blazers clinch. The next 'Red Hot Rising' is then official product.
Native American Heritage product made the Younker way: a named Oregon tribal artist, a Native-owned maker and a tribe-specific motif used with permission.
Use Portland Open Studios (Oct 10-18, 2026) and First Thursday as a scouting circuit to name a City Edition artist-in-residence for the renovation era.
watchouts: Plaid and the PDX carpet have carried four straight City Editions (2022-23 to 2025-26). A fifth will read as recycled to locals.

The White Stag sign is a city-owned historic landmark, and 'White Stag' is a separate apparel brand. Clear rights before using the sign, the stag or the name. Murals are their artists' copyright, so any reproduction, photographed walls included, needs a license.

Moda Center stands on Lower Albina land where Memorial Coliseum construction destroyed about 450 homes in a mostly Black neighborhood. Any Rose Quarter or Albina story needs Black Portland partners such as Albina Vision Trust or Vanport Mosaic as co-authors, not just references.

Avoid generic 'PNW tribal' or trade-blanket patterns. Oregon has nine federally recognized tribes. Work tribe by tribe through Native artists and Native-owned makers, and keep ceremonial imagery off product.
LAIKA's Wildwood (U.S. release Oct 23, 2026, set in Forest Park) and Rothko's paintings are third-party IP. Draw on the handmade, forest mood, not the characters or the artworks.

food.headline: Portland eats outside in the rain and still remembers the free chalupa.
food.summary: Portland eats at the cart pod, a fenced lot of independent trucks with covered seating. It cooks from an Oregon pantry that runs on the NBA clock, hazelnuts at tip-off and marionberries in July. Game day runs through the Rose Quarter, where Lillard's Spirit of 77 and the Garden Tavern pod filled up for the 2026 playoff return. The sharpest voices are Black-owned. Pay them to co-create, and mind Lillard's rival footwear deal.

insights.title: The pod is Portland's real food court
insights.detail: The Mercury's 2026 Food Issue ranked the city's top 20 standalone carts by quadrant, from Mexico City-style tacos de canasta at A Comer to Korean-Italian pasta. New pods keep opening, like Sip & Forage near PSU, built around a bar in an old bank. The Garden Tavern, a sports bar plus cart pod a few blocks from Moda Center, says it thrives in winter and is 'all about Rip City.'
insights.implication: Launch city product where Portland actually gathers. Pay a pod to run collab menu items during a City Edition reveal or opening-week drop. Design rain-ready layers for fans who eat outside under heat lamps from October to April.

insights.title: 'Cha-lu-pa!' is Blazers folk memory
insights.detail: Taco Bell handed Blazers fans more than 3 million free-food coupons whenever the team scored 100. It began in November 1999, when an Arvydas Sabonis basket against the Clippers won the first coupons, and ran to Will Barton's jumper against the Lakers in spring 2013. Fans chanted 'Cha-lu-pa!' through the fourth quarter. The McDonald's promo that replaced it never caught on.
insights.implication: The 100-point threshold and the chant are insider nostalgia from the Sabonis-to-Aldridge era. Nod to them with a coupon-stub graphic and '100' numerals on retro-leaning fan product. Leave off Taco Bell marks.

insights.title: Lillard's comeback is also a hospitality story
insights.detail: Damian Lillard returns for 2026-27 as co-owner of Spirit of 77 (500 NE MLK Jr. Blvd.), named for the 1977 title team and packed during the 2026 playoff games. He is also part-owner of Honorable Mention. That sports lounge under the Benson Hotel opened March 6, 2026, honors pioneering Black Ivy League athletes and rotates work by local Black artists each month.
insights.implication: These two rooms anchor the season's watch-party map. But Lillard has his own footwear deal with a rival brand, so work with the artists and the neighborhood around them. Don't co-brand his venues.

insights.title: Nike DNA is already inside the café scene
insights.detail: Deadstock Coffee founder Ian Williams worked his way from Nike janitor to sneaker development. Then he opened a Black-owned café lined with limited sneakers. Baristas stencil shoes into latte foam, and the slogan is 'Coffee should be dope.' He closed the Old Town storefront in December 2025 and moved into the lobby café at The Hoxton for 2026.
insights.implication: This is the best story bridge Portland offers Nike Basketball. A paid, co-credited Deadstock capsule (cup sleeves, stencil graphics, launch at The Hoxton) reaches sneaker culture and Old Town at once.

insights.title: Chef voices are Black and Haitian-American
insights.detail: Gregory Gourdet's Kann (wood-fired, gluten-free Haitian) won the James Beard Award for Best New Restaurant in 2023. Gourdet won Best Chef: Northwest in 2024. Sousòl, its basement lounge, is named for the Haitian Creole word for 'basement.' In February 2026 he brought Georgia pitmaster Bryan Furman to Portland for a limited run.
insights.implication: Gourdet is the city's most nationally credible food voice for a Black History Month or All-Star partnership. Credit and pay him, and let Haitian cultural cues come from him, not Nike.

insights.title: The Oregon pantry follows the NBA calendar
insights.detail: Chanterelles (Oregon's state mushroom) and the hazelnut harvest peak around tip-off. Commercial Dungeness crab is scheduled to open in December. OSU-bred marionberries ripen in July, during Summer League. Willamette Valley wine now has an in-arena outpost, the Domaine Serene Wine Studio.
insights.implication: Build a seasonal colorway calendar that the swap test can't break: chanterelle gold for opening night, crab-season red for holiday drops, marionberry for the summer and draft capsule.

insights.title: The concourse stays local, but the arena's future is open
insights.detail: Levy's recent Moda Center lineup added Ranch PDX square-pan pizza (every slice comes with ranch), Cha! Cha! Cha! Taqueria and Rip City Reuse returnable containers. Long-running Killer Burger, Sizzle Pie and Kama'aina poke stay. Meanwhile, owner Tom Dundon's group and the city are still negotiating a lease and a roughly $600M publicly funded renovation.
insights.implication: In-arena collab packaging and vendor-uniform capsules are realistic near-term plays. Keep the 'Moda Center' name and current vendor logos off durable product, because both could change.

places.name: Spirit of 77
places.neighborhood: Lloyd District / Rose Quarter (500 NE MLK Jr. Blvd.)
places.why: The classic pre- and post-game Blazers bar, named for the 1977 title and co-owned by Damian Lillard.

places.name: The Garden Tavern
places.kind: sports bar and food cart pod
places.neighborhood: Rose Quarter area, NE (blocks from Moda Center)
places.why: Its carts and bar depend on Blazers winters, and were packed for the 2026 playoff home games.

places.name: Moda Center concourse
places.why: Levy-run, with a lot of local vendors (Ranch PDX, Killer Burger, Sizzle Pie, Cha! Cha! Cha!, Domaine Serene) and Rip City Reuse containers.

places.name: Honorable Mention
places.why: A Lillard-backed lounge, opened March 2026, that pairs game-day screens with monthly portraits of Black athletic pioneers by local Black artists.

places.name: Deadstock Coffee at The Hoxton
places.why: A Black-owned, sneaker-walled café from an ex-Nike sneaker developer, now in the Hoxton's lobby café.

places.name: Kann / Sousòl
places.why: Gregory Gourdet's James Beard-winning Haitian restaurant and its basement cocktail lounge. The city's highest-profile Black chef platform.

places.name: Cartopia
places.why: A long-running late-night eastside pod, and a reference point for Portland's cart culture.

places.name: Prost Marketplace
places.why: A pod on the Mississippi strip, where gentrification of historically Black Albina shows block by block.

places.name: Voodoo Doughnut (Old Town)
places.why: Has repeatedly made opponent 'hex' doughnuts during Blazers playoff runs (Pelicans, Thunder, Nuggets).

people.name: Gregory Gourdet
people.role: Chef-owner, Kann and Sousòl
people.why: James Beard Best Chef: Northwest (2024) and the most nationally recognized Black chef in the city.

people.name: Damian Lillard
people.role: Blazers guard; co-owner of Spirit of 77 and part-owner of Honorable Mention
people.why: His return makes his venues the season's watch-party hubs. His footwear deal is with a rival brand.

people.name: Ian Williams (Deadstock Coffee)
people.role: Founder of Deadstock Coffee, former Nike sneaker developer
people.why: A Black Portland food entrepreneur whose story starts inside Nike.

people.name: Jr. Duperrier
people.role: Co-owner, Honorable Mention (Urban Restaurant Group)
people.why: A local Black hospitality operator behind the city's newest sports-lounge concept.

people.name: Tristan Kwame Irving
people.role: Portland artist
people.why: Painted the Fritz Pollard portrait that opened Honorable Mention's monthly series of Black athletic pioneers.

people.name: Ranch PDX
people.role: Portland square-pan pizza brand
people.why: A new Moda Center vendor whose slice-plus-ranch habit has become a game-night food.

people.name: Domaine Serene
people.role: Willamette Valley winery
people.why: Runs a wine studio inside Moda Center, bringing Oregon pinot country into the arena.

moments.name: Opening night and the new concourse lineup
moments.why: Moda Center reveals new local vendors each preseason. The 2026-27 opener is Lillard's first season back.

moments.name: Chanterelle and hazelnut harvest
moments.why: Peak Oregon-pantry season lines up with the first home games and gives the city its own fall palette.

moments.name: Dungeness crab season opener
moments.timing: Scheduled December 1 (often delayed by meat-fill testing)
moments.why: Crab feeds are a coastal Oregon holiday ritual. A hook for December and holiday product.

moments.name: Playoff watch parties and hex doughnuts
moments.why: In 2026 the Blazers hosted playoff games for the first time since 2021, and Rose Quarter bars and pods filled. Voodoo has made 'hex' doughnuts in past runs.

moments.name: Marionberry season
moments.why: Oregon's signature berry ripens during Summer League and free agency. An off-season palette.

moments.name: Honorable Mention artist rotation
moments.why: Each month features a new local Black artist's portrait of an Ivy League athletic pioneer. A source of possible art collaborators.

vocabulary.meaning: A lot where food carts cluster around shared, often covered, seating and sometimes a bar. Locals say 'meet at the pod,' not 'the food court.'
The fourth-quarter chant from 1999 to 2013, when 100 points meant free Taco Bell coupons for everyone in the building.
Long-standing nickname for Portland as a craft-beer capital.
An old nickname for Portland, and the name of the roaster whose arrival helped turn Moda Center concessions local.
Moda Center's returnable-container program at some concession stands.
Deadstock Coffee's slogan, and its no-snob, sneakerhead approach to coffee.
Haitian Creole for 'basement,' and the name of Gourdet's lounge under Kann.

designCues.cue: Chanterelle Gold: a warm apricot-gold accent for tip-off-season product.
designCues.source: The Pacific golden chanterelle, Oregon's state mushroom, foraged in fall around opening night.
designCues.use: Pair with Blazers red #E03A3E and black on tags, swooshes or piping in an October capsule.

designCues.cue: Marionberry: a near-black purple, as an alternate 'black' base.
designCues.source: The OSU-bred blackberry that ripens each July, Oregon's signature pie berry.
designCues.use: Base color for summer, draft and Summer League product, or a tonal secondary on a City Edition alternate.

designCues.cue: Filbert Husk: a toasted hazelnut-shell brown for neutrals and fleece.
designCues.source: The Willamette Valley hazelnut (filbert) orchards, which supply nearly all of the U.S. crop.
designCues.use: Fleece, cap undervisors and premium lifestyle pieces. It reads as Oregon without a logo.

designCues.cue: Perforated coupon stub with '100' numerals and a tear line.
designCues.source: The 1999–2013 Blazers 100-point free-food coupons and the 'Cha-lu-pa!' chant.
designCues.use: Use for retro tees, hangtags and ticket-style packaging. Keep it brand-free: no Taco Bell or McDonald's marks.

designCues.cue: Hand-lettered cart-menu typography: chalkboard and sign-painter scripts on corrugated metal.
designCues.source: The painted menus on Portland's cart pods, from Cartopia to the Garden Tavern.
designCues.use: Commission Portland sign painters and cart owners for capsule wordmarks. Credit and pay them, and don't fake the 'handmade' look.

designCues.cue: Sneaker-silhouette latte stencil: a top-down shoe outline in milk foam.
designCues.source: Deadstock Coffee's signature latte art.
designCues.use: Use only in a paid, co-branded Deadstock collab: cup sleeves, hoodie chest hits, a launch at The Hoxton.

designCues.cue: A returnable concession-container box made of recycled material.
designCues.source: Moda Center's Rip City Reuse program and the clamshell boxes used at the city's cart pods.
designCues.use: Packaging for city or holiday drops that fans reuse as a lunch or gear box, made with recycled content.

designCues.cue: The 'honorable mention' story: Black pioneers who earned more than a footnote.
designCues.source: The concept behind Honorable Mention and its monthly portraits by local Black artists.
designCues.use: Framing for a Black History Month capsule built with the commissioned artists themselves, not the Lillard-owned venue's brand.

productHooks: Opening-week 'Pod Pack' (water-resistant warmup jacket, shooting shirt and beanie in Chanterelle Gold, Marionberry and Filbert Husk). Launch it with a paid takeover of the Garden Tavern pod, where carts serve collab menu items.

Deadstock Coffee x Nike Basketball capsule built on Ian Williams' janitor-to-sneaker-developer story. Add a latte-stencil graphic, cup sleeves and a hoodie, launched at The Hoxton under profit-share and full co-credit.
Retro '100' fan tee and hoodie with a perforated coupon-stub graphic and Sabonis-era typography for longtime fans. No food-brand marks.
Holiday 'Crab Season' drop in December, packed in a reusable concession-style box inspired by Rip City Reuse, with crab-shell red accents on a Blazers-black base.

Black History Month capsule designed with local Black artists from Honorable Mention's portrait series (starting with Tristan Kwame Irving), story-led and artist-credited. Add a chef-hosted launch dinner with Gregory Gourdet.
watchouts: Damian Lillard has a footwear deal with a rival brand. Don't co-brand Spirit of 77 or Honorable Mention, or imply his endorsement. Work with the artists, chefs and neighborhood instead.
Taco Bell, McDonald's, Voodoo Doughnut, Stumptown, Ranch PDX and other food marks are third-party IP. Keep nostalgia graphics generic unless a deal is licensed.

Voodoo's playoff 'hex' doughnuts play on voodoo-doll caricature of Haitian Vodou, a living religion. Keep that imagery off Nike product, especially next to Haitian-American collaborators like Gourdet.

The Rose Quarter and Mississippi/Williams pods sit on historically Black Albina land cleared by urban renewal and since gentrified. Center and pay Black-owned businesses. Don't use the area as backdrop.

The Moda Center lease, renovation and naming are under negotiation, and concession and cart lineups change every year. Verify every vendor before launch. Keep arena and vendor names off long-life product.

culture.headline: Portland knows itself from the inside, and it's tired of the Portlandia version.
culture.summary: Portland sees itself as a small, rain-tested maker city that does things its own way. It assumes outsiders know it only from Portlandia sketches and 2020 protest footage. The Blazers are the city's great shared institution, and the 1977 title turns 50 on June 5, 2027. Nike's opening is a heritage year told from inside the city. Build it for drizzle and the Big Dark, and co-author it with the Black and Native Portlanders whose history sits under the Rose Quarter.

insights.title: The 1977 title turns 50 this season
insights.detail: The Blazers clinched their only championship on June 5, 1977, beating Philadelphia in Game 6 at Memorial Coliseum. That set off Blazermania and 814 straight sellouts, which ran until 1995. The 50th anniversary lands during the 2027 playoffs. Bill Walton (d. 2024), Jack Ramsay (d. 2014), Maurice Lucas (d. 2010) and Bill Schonely (d. 2023) are no longer here to tell it.
insights.implication: Make 2026-27 a heritage year. Do a 1976-77 throwback-style uniform if the team and league agree, and warmups cut to '77 proportions. Add a Blazermania 50 capsule that builds from the opener to a June 5 peak. Build it with surviving players and the estates, not just the logo vault.

insights.title: Insider pride, outsider punchline
insights.detail: Portlanders see their city as earnest, handmade and proudly odd: Mayor Bud Clark's 'Expose Yourself to Art' poster, Mill Ends Park, 'Keep Portland Weird'. They feel the country knows it through Portlandia, the 2020 protests and downtown decline. Basketball pride works the same way. There is one title and a long list of what-ifs: Sam Bowie over Michael Jordan, Greg Oden over Kevin Durant, Brandon Roy's knees. And there is Damian Lillard, who stayed 11 seasons and came back in 2025.
insights.implication: Write the product voice from inside the city. Schonely calls, loyalty and deadpan local humor land with fans. 'Put a bird on it' jokes, riot imagery and 'cursed franchise' gags read as outsiders mocking them.

insights.title: Albina is the civic story under the arena
insights.detail: Oregon was admitted in 1859 with a constitution that barred Black residents. On Memorial Day 1948 a flood wiped out Vanport, a wartime city with a large Black population. Redlining then concentrated Black Portlanders in Albina. Memorial Coliseum, I-5 and the Emanuel Hospital expansion later cleared much of Lower Albina. That is the ground under the building where the Blazers won it all.
insights.implication: Co-author and pay for any Rose Quarter, '77 or Black heritage story. Work with Oregon Black Pioneers on the history, Vanport Mosaic on Memorial Day and Albina Vision Trust on the land. Time launches to February, Memorial Day and Juneteenth, not only to game nights.

insights.title: The Northwest's team, not just Portland's
insights.detail: The Blazers are Oregon's only team in the four major men's leagues. Since the Sonics left Seattle in 2008, they have also been the only NBA team in the Pacific Northwest. Fans come from the city, from 'the Couve' (Vancouver, Wash.) and from the 541 area code, which covers most of Oregon outside the Portland-Salem corridor.
insights.implication: Make some product for Oregon as a whole: the state outline, 503 and 541, and the state flag's navy and gold, sold in Eugene, Bend and Medford. Watch the NBA's Seattle expansion closely. A revived Sonics would end the regional monopoly and start a Cascadia rivalry fans already know from Timbers vs. Sounders.

insights.title: A city of apparel insiders
insights.detail: Greater Portland built American sportswear. Jantzen swimwear (1910), White Stag skiwear and Pendleton all started here. Today it is home to Nike in Beaverton, Columbia in Washington County, adidas America in North Portland, Danner and KEEN. A large share of the Moda Center crowd works in footwear and apparel, and notices fabric, fit and who designed what.
insights.implication: Nike's hometown team needs the highest craft bar in the league, plus a credited 'designed in Rip City' story about Portland-based designers and makers. Rival brands are local here too, so compete on craft and city, not on athletes.

insights.title: Dressed for drizzle and the Big Dark
insights.detail: Portland gets only about 36 inches of rain a year, less than New York. But it arrives as months of gray drizzle, and locals skip umbrellas for hoods. The Big Dark, roughly November to February, covers the heart of the regular season. Many fans reach the Rose Quarter by MAX train or bike.
insights.implication: The real Portland fan uniform is a hoodie under a water-resistant shell. Build game-day product with DWR finishes, hoods that fit over a cap, reflective trims and packable shells. Switch to a 'sunbreak' palette in spring for the playoffs.

insights.title: Portland's fan grammar comes from soccer
insights.detail: The Timbers Army and the Thorns' Rose City Riveters set the local template for fandom: scarves, giant tifo displays, standing sections and chants. The Thorns built one of the largest crowds in women's soccer. The Portland Fire brought WNBA basketball to Moda Center in 2026, so Rip City now has a summer team.
insights.implication: Bring supporter-culture objects into Blazers product, like jacquard knit scarves and banner-scale graphics. Size Rip City pieces unisex and women's-first so Blazers and Fire fans can wear them year-round. Use each team's marks only under its own license.

places.name: Veterans Memorial Coliseum
places.why: The 1960 'Glass Palace' was the Blazers' home from 1970 to 1995 and the site of the 1977 title. It sits on Black Albina blocks cleared to build it.

places.name: Pioneer Courthouse Square
places.why: Known as 'Portland's Living Room,' it hosts the holiday tree lighting, rallies and watch parties. Its Weather Machine sculpture shows a sun, heron or dragon every day at noon.

places.name: Oregon Historical Society Museum
places.why: It holds the Portland Penny, the coin flipped in 1845 to name the city, and has shown Black Oregon history exhibitions made with Oregon Black Pioneers.

places.name: Mill Ends Park
places.why: A two-foot circle in a road median, billed as the world's smallest park, and the clearest emblem of Portland's deadpan whimsy.

places.name: Tilikum Crossing
places.why: The 2015 'Bridge of the People,' named in Chinuk Wawa, carries only trains, buses, bikes and pedestrians. Its lights shift with river conditions.

places.name: Delta Park (former Vanport)
places.why: Vanport stood here until the May 30, 1948 flood pushed Black Portland into Albina.

places.name: Japanese American Historical Plaza
places.neighborhood: Old Town / Tom McCall Waterfront Park
places.why: Cherry trees and engraved stones at the edge of the old Nihonmachi remember Japanese American incarceration. The spring bloom draws the whole city.

places.name: Jade District
places.why: The Asian American and immigrant heart of 'east of 82nd,' the city's most diverse and historically underinvested side. It rarely shows up in Portland's self-image.

places.name: NAYA Family Center
places.why: The hub of Portland's large urban Native community, and the right first call for Native-led partnerships.

places.name: Providence Park
places.why: Home of the Timbers Army and the Rose City Riveters, and where Portland's scarf, tifo and chant culture was built.

people.name: Bill Schonely
people.role: Blazers play-by-play voice from 1970 to 1998 (died 2023)
people.why: He coined 'Rip City' in the team's first season. Older fans still quote his play calls.

people.name: The 1977 Trail Blazers
people.role: NBA champions: Bill Walton, Maurice Lucas, Lionel Hollins, Bob Gross, Dave Twardzik and coach Jack Ramsay
people.why: The city's founding sports story, with its 50th anniversary on June 5, 2027. Walton, Lucas and Ramsay have died, so surviving players and the estates tell it now.

people.name: Clyde Drexler
people.role: Hall of Fame guard, Blazers 1983-95
people.why: 'Clyde the Glide' led the 1990 and 1992 Finals teams, the second Blazermania and the era Gen X fans remember.

people.name: Damian Lillard
people.role: Blazers guard, 2012-23 and again from 2025
people.why: He is Portland's loyalty story: he stayed, left and came home. He is also an adidas signature athlete, so tell the story through the city, not his likeness.

people.name: Bud Clark
people.role: Portland mayor 1985-92 and Goose Hollow Inn owner (died 2022)
people.why: He posed for 'Expose Yourself to Art' and made the great blue heron the official city bird. He set the tone for Portland's civic sense of humor.

people.name: Oregon Black Pioneers
people.role: Statewide Black history organization
people.why: It documents Black Oregon from the exclusion laws through Albina, and should co-author any Black heritage product.

people.name: Vanport Mosaic
people.role: Memory-activism nonprofit and festival
people.why: It turns the Vanport flood anniversary into a civic gathering every Memorial Day weekend.

people.name: Timbers Army and Rose City Riveters
people.role: Supporters' groups for the Timbers (MLS) and Thorns (NWSL)
people.why: They wrote Portland's rulebook for fan apparel and visual culture: scarves, tifo and DIY production.

moments.name: Home opener: the Blazermania 50 season tips off
moments.why: The first home crowd of the anniversary season and of Lillard's comeback year. The heritage story starts on night one.

moments.name: Pioneer Courthouse Square tree lighting
moments.why: Downtown's biggest annual gathering, arriving just as the Big Dark begins.

moments.name: Peacock Lane
moments.why: A Southeast Portland block that has lit up for the holidays since the 1920s. Families walk it from across the city. It is a local ritual, not a tourist one.

moments.name: Cherry blossoms at the Japanese American Historical Plaza
moments.why: The waterfront's first big outdoor crowd of spring, timed with the playoff push and the first sunbreaks.

moments.name: Vanport Mosaic Festival and Vanport flood anniversary
moments.why: Albina's founding trauma, marked in public. It is the right window for co-authored heritage work.

moments.name: Portland Rose Festival and Grand Floral Parade
moments.timing: Late May to mid-June; parade on an early-June Saturday
moments.why: Held since 1907, it is why Portland is the City of Roses. The 2027 festival overlaps the June 5 title anniversary.

moments.name: 1977 championship 50th anniversary
moments.why: Fifty years since Game 6 at Memorial Coliseum, during the 2027 playoffs.

moments.name: Hood to Coast Relay
moments.why: Running since 1982 from Mt. Hood to Seaside, it fills Oregon's NBA offseason with team-shirt culture in Nike's backyard.

vocabulary.meaning: Bill Schonely's 1971 call ('Rip City, all right!'), now the city's sporting nickname and the Blazers' rallying cry.
The fever around the 1977 title. Older fans use the word whenever the city goes all in on the team.
Schonely's play calls, like 'Bingo bango bongo' and 'Lickety brindle up the middle.' Longtime fans still quote them.
What many locals still call Moda Center, which had that name from 1995 to 2013.
The local correction for anyone who mispronounces the river, the valley or the university. Saying it right marks an insider.
Vancouver, Washington, across the Columbia. It is Blazers country, and people cross the river to shop in sales-tax-free Oregon.
Outer East Portland, the city's most diverse area, with an identity apart from the inner-city image.
The gray stretch from November to February, and the brief bright gaps between showers that forecasters and locals call sunbreaks.

designCues.cue: Big Dark slate: the flat, low cloud deck over Portland from November to February (approx. #5B636D).
designCues.source: Portland's winter sky, known locally as the Big Dark
designCues.use: A tonal base for winter fleece and shells, with Blazers red #E03A3E as a small, sharp accent.

designCues.cue: Heron blue-gray, from the great blue heron, Portland's official city bird (approx. #6C88A3).
designCues.source: Mayor Bud Clark's 1986 proclamation, and the drizzle figure on the Weather Machine
designCues.use: A secondary color for rain shells. Pair it with a small heron silhouette (long-limbed, patient, at home in the rain) as a hidden icon on a hem or jock tag.

designCues.cue: Oregon flag navy (approx. #1F2E5C) with flag gold (approx. #C9A23A).
designCues.source: The Oregon state flag
designCues.use: Use these colors for statewide product sold beyond Portland. Navy sits outside the Blazers palette, so it clearly marks the 'all of Oregon' line. Recreate the flag's colors and lettering, not the state seal.

designCues.cue: Two sides: Oregon's is the only US state flag with a different design on the back (a beaver). Portland got its name from a best-two-of-three coin flip in 1845 (the Portland Penny).
designCues.source: The Oregon flag, and the Portland Penny at the Oregon Historical Society
designCues.use: Reversible product (practice jerseys, bucket hats, bombers) with Rip City on one side and Oregon on the other, plus heads/tails hangtags.

designCues.cue: Weather Machine trio: a sun for clear skies, a great blue heron for drizzle and a dragon for storms.
designCues.source: The 1988 kinetic sculpture at Pioneer Courthouse Square, which forecasts the weather every day at noon
designCues.use: A three-icon system for seasonal drops: dragon for the Big Dark, heron for spring, sun for the playoffs. Draw them fresh rather than copying the sculpture.

designCues.cue: Glass Palace grid: the full-height glass curtain wall around Memorial Coliseum's arena bowl.
designCues.source: Veterans Memorial Coliseum (1960), the Blazers' home from 1970 to 1995 and the site of the 1977 title
designCues.use: A thin rectangular grid as a jacquard or sublimated base for 1977-anniversary warmups. The building tells the story without being named.

designCues.cue: Drizzle-grade build: a brushed-back hoodie with a DWR finish, a storm hood cut to fit over a cap, and reflective pinwheel trims.
designCues.source: Portland's no-umbrella habit, and fans who travel to games by MAX and bike
designCues.use: The base layer of game-day product. Portland fans will judge it by how it performs in the rain.

productHooks: Blazermania 50: a 1976-77 throwback-style uniform (pending team and league approval) and '77-cut warmups on a Glass Palace grid. Launch at the home opener, peak around June 5, 2027, and send proceeds to the Maurice Lucas Foundation.
'Two Sides of Oregon' reversible practice jersey and bucket hat: Rip City and 503 on one side, the state outline and 541 in Oregon navy and gold on the other. Sell it statewide, not only in Portland.

'Big Dark' game-day kit for November to February: a DWR hoodie and packable shell in slate and heron blue-gray, with a reflective pinwheel. Follow with a 'Sunbreak' colorway in March, when the mountain comes out.
An Albina heritage collection co-authored with Oregon Black Pioneers and Vanport Mosaic, designed by paid and credited Black Portland artists. Release it in February and around Memorial Day.
A 'Schonz' broadcast tee and hoodie with 'Rip City, all right!' and other Schonely calls printed inside the hem, made under an estate license for the anniversary year.
A Rip City jacquard knit scarf and a unisex fleece in one shared Portland palette. Blazers and Fire fans can both wear them, carrying Rip City from winter into the WNBA summer.
watchouts: Oregon's Black exclusion laws, Vanport and the clearing of Albina are still painful local history. Never use them as a backdrop or a slogan. Co-author that work with Black Portland institutions, and pay and credit them.

The 'Trail Blazers' name comes from Oregon Trail settler imagery. Avoid covered wagons and 'pioneer' romance, which erase the Multnomah, Clackamas, Chinook and other Native peoples. Chinuk Wawa words (Tilikum, skookum) and tribal motifs belong to living communities. Work through NAYA or specific tribes such as Grand Ronde.

Third-party IP needs permission. That covers the Portlandia statue, whose sculptor has enforced its copyright, and the Weather Machine. It covers the Cascadia 'Doug' flag, whose designer asks commercial users for permission, and Timbers, Thorns and Fire marks. It covers Pendleton patterns, and Schonely, Walton, Lucas and Ramsay likenesses, which need their estates. Recreate the ideas, and license anything reproduced.

Skip the caricatures. That means Portlandia tropes ('put a bird on it'), 2020 protest or downtown-decline imagery and 'Jail Blazers' nostalgia. It also means jokes about the Bowie or Oden 'curse' and nicknames like 'Felony Flats' for outer Southeast.
Brand conflicts: Lillard (adidas) and Aminé (New Balance) are local heroes under other brands, and adidas America is headquartered in North Portland. Check Oregon's rules before using the state seal.
