underground.headline: Portland's underground builds its own, from skateparks to supporter scarves.
underground.summary: Portland's subcultures share one ethic: do it yourself, in the rain, and don't ask first. Skaters, bike weirdos and the Timbers Army all build their own scenes. Nike is the giant next door, so the only way in is co-authorship. Skip street takeovers and keep logos out of DIY spaces. The new energy is women's sports, and the Portland Fire at Moda Center hands the Blazers a template for scarves, tifo and supporter-made product.

insights.title: Portland invented the DIY skatepark
insights.detail: Skaters began pouring Burnside under the east end of the Burnside Bridge in 1990, without permission. The city came to accept it. It became a level in the first Tony Hawk's Pro Skater and the model for Gus Van Sant's Paranoid Park. Its builders spread the Oregon concrete-park style through firms like Dreamland. The scene's uniform is Nike SB, work pants, beanies and flannel layered for rain.
insights.implication: Skate is Portland's most credible taste filter, and it already speaks Nike SB. Build a Blazers x SB crossover with Burnside-rooted skaters and pay into the park's upkeep. It will carry more street credibility here than a basketball-only drop.

insights.title: Nike's backyard turns the thrift bins into an archive
insights.detail: Nike's Beaverton campus, its employee store and the thousands of footwear designers who live here feed the thrift circuit. Samples (classically men's size 9), employee-store pickups, vintage ACG and 1990s Blazers warm-ups turn up at the Goodwill Outlet 'Bins' on SE Ochoco and on SE Hawthorne's vintage racks. With Nike and Columbia in Beaverton and Adidas North America in North Portland, the Bins and Hawthorne are among the most sportswear-literate thrift stops anywhere. Pickers prize Drexler-era and Jail Blazers-era gear (Sabonis, Stoudamire, Rasheed Wallace) and date it by the tag.
insights.implication: Portland fans know Nike better than anyone and will spot fake heritage at once. Match reissues to the archive exactly. An insider 'sample' look, with interior stamps and size callouts, is a wink only this city fully gets.

insights.title: Supporter culture lives at Providence Park, and now has a basketball outlet
insights.detail: Organized through the 107 Independent Supporters Trust, the Timbers Army and Rose City Riveters stand in the North End with knit scarves, drums, smoke and hand-painted tifo. That craft culture never grew up around the Blazers' Moda Center crowd. The Riveters' women's-sports energy found a basketball home when the WNBA's Portland Fire began play at Moda Center in 2026. Together, they make up the most celebrated supporter culture in American soccer.
insights.implication: Scarves, tifo graphics and supporter-made banners are Portland's native fan-gear language. Build Blazers versions with the city's women's-sports supporters. Remember that the Thorns (NWSL) wear Nike and the Timbers (MLS) wear Adidas.

insights.title: The bike weirdos dress for dark and wet
insights.detail: Zoobomb riders take MAX up to Washington Park, the deepest transit station in North America, then bomb the West Hills on kids' minibikes every Sunday night. Shift's Pedalpalooza fills June with hundreds of free, costumed theme rides on tall bikes and choppers. Riders wear wool and cutoffs and stick DIY reflective tape on thrifted jackets. December dusk falls before 4:30 p.m. here.
insights.implication: Reflectivity and rain-readiness are a native Portland design brief, not a gimmick. Seed a retroreflective Blazers shell to ride leaders, never as a sponsorship. It fits how this scene already customizes its gear.

insights.title: Queer nightlife and roller derby set the costume codes
insights.detail: Walter Cole performed as Darcelle until his death in 2023 at 92, the world's oldest working drag queen. Darcelle XV Showplace in Old Town still anchors the city's drag lineage. The Rose City Rollers, multiple-time WFTDA world champions, pack The Hangar at Oaks Park with skaters in pun-heavy derby names and marker-written arm numbers. The same queer, women-led crowd fills the Riveters' section at Thorns games.
insights.implication: Co-design Pride and women's-sports product with these communities, and credit and pay the performers and skaters. Derby-style custom names and numbers suit Portland-only jerseys and warm-ups.

insights.title: Albina's outdoor courts are the real hoops underground
insights.detail: Pickup runs at Irving Park in inner Northeast and the Jefferson High Democrats' program carry the basketball lineage of historically Black Albina. Portland-born pros came up through these school and park runs: Terrell Brandon (Grant), Damon Stoudamire (Wilson, now Ida B. Wells-Barnett) and Terrence Jones (Jefferson). Gentrification along Williams, Mississippi and Alberta has since displaced much of the community behind them.
insights.implication: Before any public launch, seed product and court refurbishments through Albina hoopers, coaches and community centers like Matt Dishman. Credit Black Portland basketball as the source, not a backdrop.

places.name: Burnside Skatepark
places.neighborhood: Central Eastside (under the east end of the Burnside Bridge)
places.why: The bootleg concrete park, started in 1990, that defined DIY skateboarding worldwide. It still sets Portland's street-credibility bar.

places.name: Pier Park Skatepark
places.why: One of Portland's biggest public concrete parks, and North Portland's sanctioned counterpart to Burnside's DIY original.

places.name: Irving Park courts
places.why: Outdoor courts known for competitive pickup, in the heart of historically Black Albina.

places.name: Goodwill Outlet ('the Bins'), SE Ochoco St
places.neighborhood: SE Ochoco St, on the Portland-Milwaukie line
places.why: Pay-by-the-pound bins where resellers dig for Nike samples, vintage ACG and old Blazers gear.

places.name: House of Vintage
places.why: A multi-vendor vintage warehouse that anchors the Hawthorne strip and its racks of 1990s sportswear.

places.name: Deadstock Coffee
places.why: A sneaker-themed cafe from a former Nike footwear developer, and a gathering point for Portland's sneaker-design community. It closed its Old Town storefront in December 2025 and now operates from the lobby café of The Hoxton hotel.

places.name: Providence Park North End
places.why: Home of the Timbers Army and Rose City Riveters, and the source of the city's tifo, scarf and chant culture.

places.name: Darcelle XV Showplace
places.why: Billed as the West Coast's longest-running drag showplace (since 1967), and the root of Portland's queer nightlife.

places.name: The Hangar at Oaks Park
places.why: Home track of the Rose City Rollers and their costume-heavy, women-led crowd.

places.name: Ground Kontrol Classic Arcade
places.why: Hub of Portland's arcade and pinball scene, in a city where pinball machines fill the bars and Pinball Map was born.

people.name: Rose City Rollers
people.role: Women's flat-track roller derby league, founded 2004
people.why: Its Wheels of Justice travel team are multiple-time WFTDA world champions. Its crowd is a women-led, queer-inclusive scene Nike can partner with credibly.

people.name: Timbers Army and Rose City Riveters (107 Independent Supporters Trust)
people.role: Supporter groups for the Timbers and Thorns
people.why: They set Portland's fan-gear vocabulary of scarves, tifo and chants. The Riveters back the Nike-dressed Thorns.

people.name: Zoobomb
people.role: Weekly minibike ride collective, riding since 2002
people.why: Portland's purest DIY-weird ritual. It is anti-commercial, but it defines how the city customizes gear for rain and dark.

people.name: Ian Williams (Deadstock Coffee)
people.role: Founder of Deadstock Coffee and former Nike footwear developer
people.why: He connects Portland's Black sneaker culture with the Nike design world, and is a natural host for sneaker-design workshops and drops.

people.name: Darcelle XV (Walter Cole, 1930-2023)
people.role: Drag pioneer and founder of Darcelle XV Showplace
people.why: His legacy is the spine of Portland's drag and queer nightlife history. The venue's performers carry it on.

people.name: Dreamland Skateparks (Mark 'Red' Scott)
people.role: Oregon concrete skatepark builder, founded by a Burnside veteran
people.why: It spread Burnside's poured-concrete style across Oregon, and is a credible partner for court-and-skate hybrid spaces.

people.name: Laika (Travis Knight)
people.role: Knight-family-owned stop-motion studio in Hillsboro (Coraline, Kubo and the Two Strings)
people.why: Heir to Will Vinton's Portland Claymation lineage, with a devoted animation fandom. Its film Wildwood is set in Forest Park, which makes it a ready, Nike-adjacent partner for launch films.

people.name: Damon Stoudamire
people.role: Portland-born NBA guard, Blazers 1998-2005
people.why: A Wilson High kid who came home to play point guard, he makes Jail Blazers-era vintage a hometown story, not just nostalgia. His name and likeness require retired-player licensing.

moments.name: Zoobomb
moments.why: The weekly heartbeat of Portland's bike-weird scene, and a seeding channel for rain and reflective gear.

moments.name: Timbers and Thorns home openers and Cascadia derbies
moments.timing: Late February-March openers; derbies against Seattle through the season
moments.why: The year's biggest tifo displays show the scarf-and-banner craft the Blazers can learn from.

moments.name: Rose City Rollers home season
moments.timing: Winter-spring bouts at The Hangar (confirm 2027 schedule)
moments.why: Peak visibility for derby's costume and custom-number culture, ahead of Pride.

moments.name: Nike Hoop Summit
moments.why: Nike's own elite-prospect showcase draws Portland's hoops insiders. Launch Blazers playoff-push product alongside it.

moments.name: Pedalpalooza (Shift's Bike Summer)
moments.timing: June peak, with rides into summer
moments.why: Hundreds of free themed rides where Portland shows off its DIY, customized and costumed gear.

moments.name: Portland Pride Waterfront Festival
moments.why: The citywide moment for queer-community product built with Darcelle's lineage and the derby crowd.

moments.name: Kumoricon
moments.why: Oregon's largest anime convention and the center of the city's cosplay and gaming fandom, just before Blazers preseason.

moments.name: Crafty Wonderland Holiday Market
moments.why: Portland's indie-maker marketplace, where a local-artist holiday Blazers drop would meet the city's DIY shoppers.

vocabulary.meaning: Locals mean the skatepark, not the street: 'skating Burnside'.
Riding minibikes down the West Hills from Washington Park, weekly since 2002.
Goodwill Outlet stores where unsold goods are dumped in bins and sold by the pound. 'Bin diving' is the hunt.
Pre-production Nike pairs, classically men's size 9, that leak from the campus into Portland thrift and consignment.
A friends-and-family invite to the Nike Employee Store in Beaverton, and a Portland social currency.
'Rose City 'Til I Die,' the Timbers and Thorns supporters' motto, seen on scarves, tattoos and stickers.
Nickname for the turbulent early-2000s Blazers, now affectionate shorthand among vintage hunters for that era's gear.
Rain nickname for Portland, used with pride by people who refuse umbrellas and ride anyway.

designCues.cue: Thrift-faded Blazers red
designCues.source: Sun- and wash-faded 1990s Blazers gear pulled from the Bins and the Hawthorne vintage racks.
designCues.use: Use it on garment-dyed fleece and tees, against crisp official red (#E03A3E) on jerseys. Lifestyle product reads 'found' and on-court product reads 'new'.

designCues.cue: Burnside concrete gray
designCues.source: Poured-in-place concrete under the Burnside Bridge, darkened by rain and patched by hand.
designCues.use: A speckled-heather or concrete-wash base for the SB-crossover fleece and shorts, paired with black and Blazers red.

designCues.cue: Retroreflective trim
designCues.source: Zoobomb and Pedalpalooza riders stick DIY reflective tape on thrifted jackets for pitch-dark, wet rides.
designCues.use: Reflective pinwheel stripes (the logo's two sets of five) on a rain shell and hoodie. They flash at night and stay quiet by day.

designCues.cue: Sample stamp
designCues.source: Interior 'SAMPLE' and 'NOT FOR RESALE' ink stamps and size-9 callouts on Nike samples that surface in Portland thrift.
designCues.use: Print them as interior and neck graphics on Portland-only drops. It is Nike's own visual language, so there is no licensing risk.

designCues.cue: Supporters' scarf jacquard
designCues.source: Knit bar scarves raised in the North End at Providence Park and in the Riveters' section.
designCues.use: A two-sided jacquard Blazers scarf and knit trims, co-designed with women's-sports supporters. Avoid Timbers green-and-gold and any Timbers or MLS marks.

designCues.cue: Hand-painted tifo and derby lettering
designCues.source: Supporter-painted giant banners and derby skaters' marker-written numbers.
designCues.use: Brush lettering for 'Rip City' and custom numbers on shooting shirts. Commission the supporter and derby artists themselves rather than imitating them.

designCues.cue: Built without permission
designCues.source: Burnside, 1990: skaters poured concrete under the bridge before the city said yes.
designCues.use: The hangtag and launch story for a skate crossover. Let the skaters tell it, and never imply Nike had a hand in it.

designCues.cue: Shell-over-jersey layering
designCues.source: Portland's hood-up, no-umbrella habit, and ACG, which launched from Beaverton in 1989.
designCues.use: A packable hooded shell cut roomy enough to layer over a jersey, for walking to Moda Center in November rain.

productHooks: Burnside x Blazers via Nike SB: concrete-gray (#8D8C87) speckle fleece and skate-durable shorts with pinwheel stripes, designed with Burnside-rooted skaters. A share of proceeds goes to park upkeep through a group the skaters choose. No logos at the park.

'Portland Sample' drop: tees and hoodies with sample-stamp interior prints and faded-red (#C9584F) garment dye. Sell it only at Portland doors and Moda Center, a love letter to the city that hunts samples at the Bins.
Rip City supporters' kit: a jacquard scarf and tifo-print shooting shirt, co-designed with Portland women's-sports supporters (Riveters and Fire fans) and released for the first home playoff game.

'Night Ride' Blazers rain shell: an ACG-built hooded shell with retroreflective pinwheel stripes. Drop it in November, when dusk falls before 5 p.m., and seed it, don't sponsor it, to Zoobomb and Shift ride leaders.

Pride warm-up co-designed with Rose City Rollers skaters and Darcelle XV performers, with derby-style custom names and numbers. Credit and pay the creators, and send proceeds to a local LGBTQ+ organization they pick.
Hometown 1990s reissue: archive-exact Drexler- and Stoudamire-era Blazers warm-ups with period tags and details, pending retired-player licensing.
watchouts: Brand conflict: the Timbers wear Adidas (MLS-wide deal), Adidas North America is headquartered in North Portland, and the Timbers Army has a history of political-banner fights with MLS. Engage the Nike-dressed Thorns, the Riveters and the Fire, not Timbers Army branding.
Burnside, Zoobomb and Pedalpalooza are proudly non-commercial. Never brand the spaces or name products after them without explicit permission. Seed and fund, don't sponsor.

Nike is in Beaverton, not Portland, and Phil Knight's multimillion-dollar donations in recent Oregon elections are a live talking point in these left-leaning scenes. Lead with paid, credited local partners.

Leave street takeovers and sideshows alone. They are illegal and a city enforcement priority. Handle 'Jail Blazers' with care because it references player arrests, and license any retired player's name or likeness.
Queer, derby and Black Albina cues must come from partnership, credit and pay. Avoid 'Keep Portland Weird' kitsch and gentrifier aesthetics on the Williams, Mississippi and Alberta corridors.

hoops.headline: In Portland, every pro comes with a high school attached.
hoops.summary: Portland's basketball identity was built in the Portland Interscholastic League. Jefferson, Grant, Benson, Franklin and Wilson (now Ida B. Wells-Barnett) produced Ime Udoka, Terrell Brandon, A.C. Green, the Schimmel sisters and Damon Stoudamire. Rain sets the calendar, and the city now has three pro teams. Nike's opening is Portland-only product that starts in PIL gyms and on Albina courts, and credits the people who built them.

insights.title: Two hometown brands, one backcourt
insights.detail: Nike and Jordan Brand are headquartered in Beaverton, and adidas North America sits on N Greeley Ave in North Portland. Local gyms mix Beaverton samples and early releases with Dame sneakers. In 2026-27 Lillard (adidas) shares the Blazers' backcourt with Ja Morant, who has a Nike signature line. The brand rivalry is now a home-team storyline.
insights.implication: Lead Portland product with Morant and the team, never with Lillard's personal adidas marks. Then compete for the gyms and courts where both companies' families and employees play.

insights.title: The PIL is the pipeline, and locals claim pros by high school
insights.detail: Portlanders tag their pros by school first: Jefferson's Ime Udoka and Terrence Jones, Grant's Terrell Brandon, Benson's A.C. Green, Franklin's Aaron Brooks and Wilson's Damon Stoudamire, who came home to play for the Blazers from 1998 to 2005. Even Domantas Sabonis gets claimed. He was born in Portland in 1996 while his father Arvydas played for the Blazers. Albina's Matt Dishman Community Center and Irving Park are the neighborhood runs.
insights.implication: Make the school the unit of the story. Do school-licensed warm-ups, gym refurbishments and athlete stories that name the high school. Credit the Black Albina coaches and families who built the Jefferson and Grant programs.

insights.title: City versus suburbs is the rivalry that matters
insights.detail: The PIL's inner-city public schools measure themselves against the Catholic powers, Central Catholic and Jesuit, and against suburban 6A programs like West Linn (Payton Pritchard) and Lake Oswego (Kevin Love). Love chose UCLA over his father's alma mater, Oregon, and got heckled at McArthur Court in Eugene.
insights.implication: Keep Portland-city product rooted in the PIL and Albina. Suburban and private-school programs are a different Portland. Blend them into one generic 'Rip City kid' and it rings false to both.

insights.title: Women's hoops is the second engine
insights.detail: The WNBA's Portland Fire revived the name of the 2000-02 franchise and finished its first season at Moda Center in 2026. Oregon's Sabrina Ionescu-era teams and the Thorns had already shown how hard the state shows up for women's sports. Franklin High's Shoni Schimmel was MVP of the 2014 WNBA All-Star Game.
insights.implication: Nike makes every WNBA uniform, so the Fire is a second Nike-made home team. Design Rip City product women's-first and keep it selling from May through September, when the Blazers are off.

insights.title: Rain writes the calendar, and summer has a pro-am gap
insights.detail: Portland's wet season runs roughly October to May. Winter pickup moves into community-center gyms like Matt Dishman and under school covered play areas. Outdoor runs at courts like Irving Park peak in the reliably dry July-September window. No Portland summer league has the national weight of Seattle's Crawsover Pro-Am.
insights.implication: Drop outdoor court-wear in July and layered warm-ups in October. Fund a free summer run at Irving Park with Albina organizers. It fills the pro-am gap with something local, not imported.

insights.title: Nike's own stage is already in town
insights.detail: The Nike Hoop Summit has played at Moda Center most Aprils since 2008. The Les Schwab Invitational brings national high school powers to Hillsboro between Christmas and New Year's. The OSAA 6A state finals fill UP's Chiles Center in March. The G League Rip City Remix also plays at Chiles.
insights.implication: Make Hoop Summit week the anchor event. It is Nike's event in Nike's home market. Use it for Portland-only drops and PIL youth clinics run by local coaches, then follow up with Les Schwab in winter and the state finals in spring.

insights.title: Portland talks hoops through its own outlets
insights.detail: The Blazers left Root Sports in 2024 and built their own over-the-air and streaming setup. Independent coverage runs through SB Nation's Blazer's Edge and Sean Highkin's Rose Garden Report. Its name keeps alive what locals still call the arena, the Rose Garden (renamed Moda Center in 2013).
insights.implication: Seed launches with Portland beat writers and creators before national outlets. 'Rose Garden'-era references, like 1990s and 2000s warm-ups, read as in-group nostalgia to lifelong fans.

Short for the Jefferson High Democrats, Albina's flagship basketball program.

designCues.cue: Wet-asphalt slate: the near-black of an outdoor court after an October drizzle, with painted lines glowing white under park lights
designCues.source: Irving Park and Northeast neighborhood courts through Portland's October-May wet season.
designCues.use: Base color for an outdoor-court capsule, paired with reflective white line graphics. The hex is an approximation, so match it to a lab dip.

designCues.cue: Rip City red as the single saturated hit on slate
designCues.source: The Blazers' red, which has run from the 1977 Blazermania team to every Portland gym and park court.
designCues.use: Use it only on taping, drawcords, a pinwheel-stripe hem or inside plackets, so the slate base reads as Portland weather. Use it under the NBA and Blazers license.

designCues.cue: Ducks green, the color of the state's Nike-backed flagship program
designCues.source: University of Oregon, Phil Knight's alma mater and a long-running Nike uniform test bed.
designCues.use: Use UO marks only under a university license. Without marks, use a fir green as an Oregon-pride accent on statewide pieces.

designCues.cue: Fir line: a continuous row of Douglas-fir silhouettes running along a baseline
designCues.source: Oregon's state tree, and the 'Deep in the Woods' court Tinker Hatfield designed for Matthew Knight Arena in 2011.
designCues.use: Use it as a hem print on shorts or a shooting-shirt yoke. Draw original firs rather than copying UO's court art.

designCues.cue: Claimed by school: a two-tier chest lockup with the high school's name stacked over RIP CITY
designCues.source: Portlanders identify their pros by PIL school first (Jefferson, Grant, Benson, Franklin, Wells).
designCues.use: Use it for PIL team warm-ups and licensed retail versions, set in each school's own varsity lettering and approved by the school.

designCues.cue: Play-shed layer: a hooded shooting shirt with water-repellent shoulders, a mesh back panel and a drop-tail hem
designCues.source: Rain pushes Portland runs under school covered play areas and into drafty community gyms, with a wet walk in and out.
designCues.use: Use it as the uniform for a summer run and as Fire and Blazers warm-ups. Build it in Storm-FIT-type fabric so it works as pregame and street wear.

designCues.cue: Off the Rez: the Schimmel sisters' path from the Umatilla Reservation to Franklin High, Louisville and the WNBA
designCues.source: Shoni and Jude Schimmel and the documentary 'Off the Rez', a defining Northwest Native basketball story.
designCues.use: Use only as a co-authored capsule with the Schimmels and paid, credited artists chosen with the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation. No sacred or ceremonial imagery, and no generic 'tribal' patterns.

watchouts: Brand conflict: Damian Lillard is an adidas signature athlete, and adidas North America is headquartered in North Portland. Keep 'Dame Time', 'Dame D.O.L.L.A.' and his signature marks off Nike product. Check whether adidas or Lillard have refurbished any Portland court before Nike touches it.

Vet every athlete partner. Ja Morant served NBA suspensions in 2023 for displaying guns in social videos, and Ime Udoka was suspended by the Celtics in 2022. Do a brand-safety review before any Portland-specific or youth-facing product.

Gentrification along Williams, Mississippi and Alberta has displaced Albina's Black basketball community. Credit and pay Albina coaches, families and organizers, and don't use their courts as a backdrop for outsiders. Keep 'Jail Blazers' and its arrest history off product.
Native hoops: partner with the Schimmels and CTUIR-approved artists, and pay and credit them. Use no sacred or ceremonial imagery, and no Pendleton-style patterns without a license.

Licensing and minors: UO, Oregon State, UP, PPS and PIL school marks, plus OSAA, Les Schwab, Fire and Remix marks, all need licenses. Never feature high school athletes by name or likeness without consent and OSAA compliance.

fanbase.headline: Lillard comes home, Morant arrives, and fans haven't decided about the owner.
fanbase.summary: Blazers fans don't do bandwagons. They back Oregon's only team in the four major men's leagues and still quote the 814 straight sellouts. They open 2026-27 hopeful but guarded. Last season ended 42-40, with a play-in win over Phoenix and a first-round exit, and now there's a first-year coach in Micah Nori and an unsigned lease. The franchise icon wears adidas, so Nike's opening is the fans' own story.

insights.title: Loyalty is the core value, and Lillard tested it both ways
insights.detail: Lillard spent 11 seasons in Portland, asked for a trade in 2023, and re-signed in July 2025 after Milwaukee waived him with a torn Achilles. He missed all of 2025-26, so this is his first season in a Blazers uniform since spring 2023. Fans called it a homecoming, not a betrayal forgiven.
insights.implication: The #0 jersey is the Nike item most worth planning around here. Stock it deep in every edition for his first home game. Build homecoming graphics from team and city marks (Rip City, the pinwheel), not Lillard's own.

insights.title: Two shoe brands in one backcourt, in Nike's hometown
insights.detail: Lillard has been an adidas signature athlete since early in his career, and adidas North America's campus sits in North Portland, minutes from the Moda Center. Morant wears Nike's Ja line. Nike makes the uniform they both play in.
insights.implication: A red-and-black Blazers Ja colorway is Nike's most direct on-court play in Portland. Let the jersey and fan gear unite the two guards. Never frame product as a Nike-versus-adidas fight between them.

insights.title: The Jail Blazers memory makes conduct part of the deal
insights.detail: In the early 2000s, arrests and open hostility toward fans on the "Jail Blazers" teams emptied seats. The front office answered with a public 25-point pledge to fans in 2003, then rebuilt around high-character stars Brandon Roy and Lillard. Morant arrives with two 2023 NBA suspensions over firearm videos.
insights.implication: Lead Morant product with basketball and Portland. Skip edgy, "villain" or weapon-adjacent cues. Let his early-season play and visible community work earn the bigger drops.

insights.title: Fans kept the team here, and now they're judging the owner
insights.detail: Dundon bought the team in March 2026. Oregon, Multnomah County and Portland have committed $586M toward roughly $600M in Moda Center upgrades. The lease is unsigned, and Dundon has said he won't pay for the work. Fans are relieved the Blazers are staying while Seattle chases expansion. They're wary of an owner whose Carolina Hurricanes tenure earned a reputation for frugality.
insights.implication: Center product on the fans and the city that paid to keep the team. Treat Rip City as a civic name, not a new-regime slogan. Hold "new era" messaging until the lease is done.

insights.title: The game-day uniform is a jersey over a hoodie, under a shell
insights.detail: The season runs through the November-to-February Big Dark, and many fans reach the Rose Quarter by MAX. The look is a red or black hoodie with the jersey pulled over it, or over a long-sleeve, plus a rain shell and a knit beanie. A jersey over a T-shirt mostly shows up at playoff and spring games.
insights.implication: Cut fan pieces for layering: jerseys with room for a hoodie, hooded long-sleeve shooters, and shells long enough to cover a Swingman. Ship them in team colors before the Big Dark sets in.

insights.title: Fans dress by era, and this season has no new City story
insights.detail: Lifers wear 1977 Walton and Lucas, the 1990 and 1992 Finals teams (Drexler, Porter, Kersey, with the diagonal stripe), Sabonis and Brandon Roy. The team re-wears its 2019-20 City Edition in 2026-27. The 1977 title turns 50 on June 5, 2027, in the middle of the playoffs.
insights.implication: Fill the gap with heritage: a '77-inspired Classic Edition or warmup if the team and league agree, plus era-blend fan graphics. Mitchell & Ness largely owns vintage replicas, so Nike's lane is new design built on the old cues.

places.name: Moda Center
places.why: Home since 1995 and still "the Rose Garden" to fans. Its publicly funded renovation and unsigned lease make it this season's civic flashpoint.

places.name: Veterans Memorial Coliseum
places.why: The "Glass Palace" where Blazermania began and the 1977 title was clinched in Game 6. In a 50th-anniversary year, it's the shrine for lifers.

places.name: Spirit of 77
places.neighborhood: Lloyd District / Rose Quarter (500 NE MLK Jr. Blvd.)
places.why: Named for the title team and a short walk from the arena, it's the default pregame stop and road-game watch party. It was packed during the 2026 playoff run.

places.name: Nike Community Store
places.why: Nike's long-running Northeast Portland store hires from the surrounding neighborhood. It's the natural door for a community-first Blazers drop.

places.name: Matt Dishman Community Center
places.why: A historic Albina rec center and gym at the center of Black Portland's youth hoops, and the right venue for clinics tied to Blazers moments.

places.name: Jefferson High School
places.why: The Democrats are the signature hoops program of the historic Black community, followed in Albina almost as closely as the Blazers.

places.name: Irving Park
places.why: Northeast Portland's most storied outdoor run, where summer pickup ties Albina hoops culture to Blazers fandom.

places.name: Providence Park
places.why: The Timbers Army and Rose City Riveters wrote Portland's supporter grammar of scarves, tifo and chants. Blazers fans borrow from it.

people.name: Damian Lillard
people.role: Blazers guard (2012-23, 2025-), adidas signature athlete, rapper Dame D.O.L.L.A.
people.why: The franchise's loyalty symbol, back from a torn Achilles. His #0 is Nike's biggest jersey opportunity here, but his shoe and personal marks sit with adidas.

people.name: Ja Morant
people.role: Blazers guard, acquired from Memphis on June 29, 2026; Nike signature athlete
people.why: Nike's on-court hook in its hometown. Fans are weighing his talent against two 2023 suspensions and a possible bench role under Nori.

people.name: Deni Avdija
people.role: Blazers forward from Israel, acquired from Washington in 2024
people.why: Embraced as the all-around engine of the rebuild after Lillard's exit, and a draw for an international following.

people.name: Toumani Camara
people.role: Blazers forward from Belgium
people.why: A defense-first fan favorite in the Kersey and Lucas mold. He came in the 2023 Lillard trade, and Jrue Holiday, also part of that deal, is back after a later return to Portland. Dame returns to a roster partly built from his own exit.

people.name: Tom Dundon
people.role: Blazers owner since March 2026; also owns the Carolina Hurricanes
people.why: Fans credit the sale and the public arena money with keeping the team in Portland. His refusal to pay for the renovation keeps them wary, so don't center product on him.

people.name: Portland Gear (Marcus Harvey)
people.role: Black-owned Portland apparel brand
people.why: Its "Portland" graphics are what many fans wear around town instead of team merch. That makes it the clearest candidate for a credited, paid local collaboration.

people.name: Blazer's Edge and r/ripcity
people.role: SB Nation fan site and the team's subreddit
people.why: Where diehards argue rotations and grade every jersey release. It's the fastest read on whether a Blazers drop lands.

people.name: Self Enhancement, Inc. (SEI)
people.role: NE Portland youth-development nonprofit
people.why: A long-standing Albina institution and a natural paid partner for events built with Black Portland families.

moments.name: Lillard's first Moda Center game back in a Blazers uniform
moments.why: His first game for Portland since spring 2023, and the season's biggest jersey and game-day apparel moment.

moments.name: NBA Cup group play, West Group C
moments.why: A group with San Antonio, the Lakers, Golden State and Sacramento brings a Spurs rematch and "Beat L.A." energy to the early season.

moments.timing: Every Lakers game at Moda Center (2026-27 dates to confirm)
moments.why: The loudest regular-season crowd of the year, and the natural release date for chant-driven fan gear.

moments.name: Play-in and playoff push, plus the Dame-shot anniversaries
moments.timing: April 2027 (April 23 for the 2019 shot over OKC, May 2 for the 2014 shot at 0.9 seconds against Houston)
moments.why: Fans relive both series-winners every spring while chasing a second straight postseason.

moments.name: Portland Fire WNBA season
moments.why: Keeps Rip City crowds in the Moda Center through the summer. It's a cross-sell to the same fans and a strong audience for women's fits.

moments.name: 50th anniversary of the 1977 title
moments.why: The fan base's founding myth turns 50, in the middle of the playoffs.

vocabulary.meaning: Bill Schonely's 1971 call, now the city's sporting name. Fans shout it, wear it and sign off with it.
The 1977 title fever and the sellout era it started. Lifers use it as shorthand for "real" fandom.
Lillard's late-game takeover, signaled by tapping the wrist. Fans do it in the stands, though the phrase belongs to his personal brand.
The chant for every Lakers visit, sharpened by the 2000 Western Conference finals Game 7 collapse.
The fourth-quarter chant from 1999 to 2013, when scoring 100 won fans a free-food coupon. It now runs on nostalgia.
What many fans still call the Moda Center, the arena's name from 1995 to 2013.
The early-2000s teams known for arrests and feuds with fans. Fans say it with a wince, as a warning.
Fans' name for the 1970 logo: five red and five white stripes, for two teams of five.

designCues.cue: Rip City red, the official Blazers red (#E03A3E), at full saturation.
designCues.source: The team's core color since 1970 and the hoodie color of every Big Dark crowd
designCues.use: Make it the lead color for fan fleece and beanies. On black shells, limit it to linings, zip pulls and the pinwheel so it reads as a sharp signal.

designCues.cue: Blazers black (#000000), the base of the Lillard-era fan wardrobe.
designCues.source: The black jerseys, hoodies and Rip City tees that dominate the lower bowl
designCues.use: The base for outerwear and layering pieces, so a red jersey or pinwheel pops over it.

designCues.cue: The slash: the diagonal red-black-white stripe across the Blazers jersey front.
designCues.source: Blazers uniforms from the Drexler-era Finals teams to today
designCues.use: Run it across hoodie chests, shell yokes and beanie cuffs. It says Portland without a logo.

designCues.cue: The pinwheel, five-and-five: two interlocking sets of five stripes.
designCues.source: The 1970 logo, which fans call the pinwheel
designCues.use: Use it as a reflective hood mark, zip pull or embroidered hem tag. It's a small signature that shows in the rain for MAX riders.

designCues.cue: 814: the sellout streak as a numeral, with fans as the roster.
designCues.source: The 814 consecutive sellouts from 1977 to 1995
designCues.use: A fan-side number for tees and scarves that celebrates the crowd, not any player's personal brand.

designCues.cue: Chant typography: "BEAT L.A.!" and "RIP CITY" in heavy condensed capitals, set like a homemade bedsheet sign.
designCues.source: Moda Center chants and fan signs
designCues.use: Drop chant tees for Lakers nights and Cup games, and keep the exclamation-point energy.

designCues.cue: Jersey-over-hoodie layering: a roomier jersey or hooded shooter cut to sit over fleece.
designCues.source: How Portland fans wear jerseys through eight wet months
designCues.use: Make layering-friendly fits and hooded long-sleeve jerseys the fan silhouette here, not the summer tank.

designCues.cue: Red-and-black buffalo check flannel.
designCues.source: Pacific Northwest wool and workwear worn in the upper bowl and around town
designCues.use: Use it for shell linings or a shirt-jacket with a pinwheel patch. Draw an original check, never a Pendleton pattern.

productHooks: Homecoming #0: deep Lillard #0 Swingman stock in Association, Icon, Statement and the re-worn 2019-20 City Edition for his first home game. Add a fan-voice Rip City homecoming tee built only from team marks.
A Blazers red-and-black colorway of Morant's current Ja signature shoe. Start with a player exclusive, then a retail drop timed to NBA Cup nights once he has settled in.
814 Club fan capsule: chant tees, knit beanies and supporter-style scarves honoring the sellout streak and "Beat L.A.!", released for Lakers visits.

Big Dark game-day shell: packable, water-resistant and black, with a reflective red pinwheel, a storm hood that fits over a cap and a hem long enough to cover a Swingman. Sell it at the Moda Center, the Nike Community Store and statewide doors for 541 fans.
An Albina community capsule co-designed and credited with Black Portland creators such as Portland Gear. Proceeds go to SEI or Jefferson hoops. Release it in February or around Juneteenth.
watchouts: Lillard's shoe and personal marks ("Dame Time", "Dame D.O.L.L.A.", his logo) sit with adidas or with him. Stick to his jersey and team marks unless a license is cleared.
Given the Jail Blazers memory and Morant's 2023 suspensions, avoid "villain", edgy or weapon-adjacent styling. Be ready to pause Ja-Portland product if conduct issues return.
Ownership and the arena deal divide fans: public money, an unsigned lease, an owner who won't pay for the renovation. Keep product about the fans and the city, not the new regime.
Celebrate Avdija as a Blazer, without national or political symbolism. Portland has an active protest culture, and anything read as a geopolitical statement will backfire.
Rip City and the pinwheel are team marks, and Cha-lu-pa! is tied to a Taco Bell promotion. Albina cues must be co-created with, credited to and paid to Black Portland creators, never borrowed.

segments.name: Blazermania lifers
segments.description: Season-ticket holders and longtime fans, mostly boomers and Gen X, whose fandom runs from 1977 through the 1990 and 1992 Finals. They value loyalty, history and good conduct.
segments.share: Largest share of the seats in the building
segments.wears: Vintage Drexler #22 and Porter #30, Walton and '77 tees, Starter-era jackets, a red beanie and a rain shell.
segments.reach: Season-ticket events, the radio broadcast, the Oregonian and Blazer's Edge, and heritage nights at Veterans Memorial Coliseum.

segments.name: The Dame generation
segments.description: Millennials and Gen Z who grew up on Lillard from 2012 to 2023 and followed the young core through the lottery years. They're curious about Morant, mostly digital and hungry for playoffs.
segments.share: Largest online, and growing in the building
segments.wears: A #0 jersey in every edition, layered over a hoodie, with player tees, signature sneakers from both brands and Nike Tech.
segments.reach: r/ripcity, team TikTok and Instagram, Blazers podcasts, and watch parties at Spirit of 77.

segments.name: Albina and NE Portland hoops community
segments.description: Black Portlanders and families with roots in Albina, many now pushed east by gentrification, tied to Jefferson, Dishman and Irving Park hoops. They value investment in the community and in local creators.
segments.wears: Portland Gear and other local Black-owned brands, Nike from the Community Store, and current-player and Lillard jerseys.
segments.reach: Through paid partners such as SEI, Jefferson High, Dishman and local creators, never cold outreach.

segments.name: Industry insiders
segments.description: Footwear and apparel workers from Nike, adidas, Columbia and their agencies. They read every uniform for fabric, fit and who designed it.
segments.share: Outsized for a single NBA crowd
segments.wears: Samples, employee-store finds, player-exclusive shoes and technical outerwear. They'll spot a lazy template.
segments.reach: Internal design networks, the Pensole and other design-school crowds, and limited drops with credited designer stories.

segments.name: Oregon and SW Washington regional fans
segments.description: Fans in the 541 (Eugene, Bend, Medford) and in Salem and Vancouver, Wash., for whom the Blazers are the only NBA team in the Northwest. Mostly families who watch on TV and make one or two trips a season.
segments.wears: Red tees, caps and beanies from statewide retailers, plus flannel and outdoor shells, often paired with Ducks or Beavers gear.
segments.reach: Regional broadcasts and radio, statewide retail such as Fred Meyer, and road-trip family packages.

segments.name: International and diaspora followers
segments.description: Fans of Avdija (Israel), Camara (Belgium) and Sharpe (Canada), plus Lithuanians who still claim Sabonis.
segments.wears: Player jerseys and name-and-number tees bought online.
segments.reach: NBA League Pass and the team's social channels, with player-specific content around road trips and international windows.

traditions.name: 'Rip City!'
traditions.detail: Schonely's 1971 call, now a call-and-response from the PA and the team's signature on towels, signs and the floor.

traditions.name: 'Beat L.A.!'
traditions.detail: The chant for every Lakers game, still fueled by the 15-point fourth-quarter lead lost in Game 7 of the 2000 Western Conference finals.

traditions.name: 'Cha-lu-pa!'
traditions.detail: From 1999 to 2013 the crowd chanted for the 100th point and its free-food coupon. Fans still revive it on nostalgia nights.

traditions.name: The wrist tap
traditions.detail: Fans tap their wrists for Dame Time in clutch moments. Expect the ritual to return with Lillard.

traditions.name: Blaze the Trail Cat
traditions.detail: The mascot since 2002, known for trampoline dunks during timeouts and a fixture of family nights.

traditions.name: MAX in, Spirit of 77 first
traditions.detail: Fans ride MAX to the Rose Quarter in rain gear and pregame at nearby bars. There's no tailgating culture.

icons.name: Jerome Kersey

icons.name: Arvydas Sabonis
icons.why: The Lithuanian giant fans waited nine years for, and a cult hero of the Rose Garden's early days.

icons.name: Brandon Roy
icons.why: "B-Roy" rebuilt trust after the Jail Blazers era. Fans remember his 2011 Game 4 comeback against Dallas and still mourn his knees.

icons.name: Damian Lillard
icons.why: Hit the 0.9-second shot in 2014 and the "wave goodbye" shot in 2019, stayed through the lean years, then came home.

rivalries.why: The 2000 Game 7 collapse, Lakers fans who travel well to Portland, and a "Beat L.A." chant that never retired. They're also in the Blazers' 2026 NBA Cup group.
The I-5 rivalry went dormant when the Sonics left in 2008. It would reignite if Seattle gets an expansion team.
They ended Portland's season 4-1 in both 2014 and 2026, and they share the 2026 NBA Cup group.
Lillard's 2019 series-ending shot over Paul George and the "wave goodbye" are canon. The Thunder also carry the old Sonics lineage.

extra.sentiment: Hopeful but guarded. Fans welcomed the 2026 playoff return after four lottery seasons and an interim year that began with Chauncey Billups' arrest. They're excited about Lillard's comeback and split on Morant: talent against conduct and health history. They debate Nori's possible bench role for one of the two guards and see a 43.5-win line as fair. Relief that public money keeps the team in Portland sits next to wariness of Dundon and the unsigned lease.
extra.gamedayLook: A red or black Blazers hoodie with a #0 Lillard jersey pulled over it, under a rain shell. Avdija and Sharpe shirts are rising, and Morant gear is just arriving. Add a red knit beanie or flat-brim cap, jeans or joggers, and Nike or adidas runners or boots. Older fans swap in Drexler #22, '77 Walton tees and red-and-black flannel.

rhythm.headline: The Blazers get Portland through the Big Dark, with peaks in October and April.
rhythm.summary: Portland's fan year follows the weather. The NBA season fills the wet, dark half of the year, when the city moves indoors, and August is the low point. This season peaks twice. October brings Lillard's return and Morant's first games, and April decides a team with a 43.5-win total. With no opening-night or Christmas game, local dates carry the calendar, all the way to June 5, 2027.

insights.title: The NBA season is Portland's indoor season
insights.detail: Rain usually returns in mid-October. Daylight saving ends on Nov 1, 2026, and sunset jumps overnight from about 6:01 to about 4:59 pm. By early December the sun sets around 4:27 pm. Every 7 pm tip from November through February is in rain and full dark. Once the dry season starts in July, Portland heads for the Willamette, the Gorge, Mt. Hood and the coast.
insights.implication: Launch weatherproof Blazers product with the Nov 1 clock change, not on opening night. In July and August, sell lifestyle and outdoor product ahead of team gear.

insights.title: Two peaks in 2026-27: October hope, April verdict
insights.detail: October brings Lillard's first season back after missing all of 2025-26 and Morant's debut after the June 29 trade. Micah Nori must decide whether one of them comes off the bench. The Oct 30 Cup opener against Golden State follows. Last season ended 42-40, with a 114-110 play-in win over Phoenix and a 4-1 first-round loss to San Antonio. With a 43.5-win total, April likely comes down to a play-in again.
insights.implication: Put jersey and outerwear inventory into October. For April, hold a ready-to-print playoff run that can scale up or be cancelled within days of the standings settling.

insights.title: Off the national calendar, so local dates carry the year
insights.detail: Portland misses the Oct 20 opening-night tripleheader, the Christmas Day slate and NBC's MLK Day quadrupleheader. Its biggest nights are local: the home opener, Friday Cup games against the Spurs, Lakers, Warriors and Kings, and Thanksgiving week. Re-wearing the 2019-20 City Edition also means no new City Edition launch this fall.
insights.implication: Build the drop calendar around the home opener, Nov 1, Black Friday (Nov 27) and June 5, not league tentpoles. Treat Christmas as a ship-by deadline, not a game. Fill the November-December launch slot a new City Edition would normally take with a heritage capsule.

insights.title: June is the hidden second peak: Blazermania 50
insights.detail: The Blazers clinched their only title on June 5, 1977, at Memorial Coliseum. June 5, 2027 is a Saturday in the Rose Festival window. Juneteenth (Sat June 19) and Father's Day (Sun June 20) weekend follows two weeks later. A month that usually belongs to other teams' Finals can belong to Portland.
insights.implication: Run a season-long Blazermania 50 countdown that peaks in June, with Father's Day heritage product for the generation that lived 1977. Build it with surviving players and the estates.

insights.title: Rip City has a summer shift now
insights.detail: The WNBA's Portland Fire play at Moda Center from May to September. The Timbers and Thorns play at Providence Park from February to November. The Rose Festival and the July 4th-weekend Waterfront Blues Festival fill Waterfront Park. Portland stays busy when the Blazers are off.
insights.implication: Sell women's-first, lightweight Rip City product from May to September so the summer isn't dead. Each team's marks need their own license.

insights.title: The Ducks own Oregon's fall Saturdays
insights.detail: Oregon Ducks football is a Big Ten and College Football Playoff contender that can hold Saturdays into January. Portland has no NFL team, so Sundays go to the Seahawks. From December to March, Mt. Hood ski weekends pull away the fans with the most money to spend. Blazers home games mostly own weeknights.
insights.implication: Launch Blazers product around weeknight home games and steer clear of big Ducks Saturdays. Keep Oregon-wide product (503/541, state outline) for fans outside the Portland metro.

insights.title: When Portland buys
insights.detail: December holiday gifting drives the most units, April playoff runs drive the sharpest team-gear spike, and August is the low point. Local makers such as Portland Gear can have playoff tees on the street within days of a big win.
insights.implication: Nike's edge is having product ready before the moment: jerseys before winter break, red playoff blanks before the play-in, a heritage line for June. Partner with local printers on speed instead of trying to beat them at it.

places.name: Moda Center
places.why: Hosts the Blazers from October to April and the Fire from May to September, so the building works most of the year. Locals still call it the Rose Garden.

places.name: Veterans Memorial Coliseum
places.why: Where the 1977 title was won on June 5, 1977, and home to the WHL's Winterhawks from September to March. It's the obvious site for a June 5, 2027 anniversary moment.

places.name: Rose Quarter Transit Center
places.why: The MAX stop most fans walk from to Moda Center, often in November rain and dark. A natural place to show weatherproof game-night product.

places.name: Pioneer Courthouse Square
places.why: "Portland's living room" hosts the tree lighting the day after Thanksgiving. In 2026 that's Nov 27, the Blazers' last Cup Friday and Black Friday.

places.name: Tom McCall Waterfront Park
places.why: Hosts Rose Festival CityFair in late May and June and the Waterfront Blues Festival on July 4th weekend. It's the city's summer gathering place when the Blazers are off.

places.name: Providence Park
places.why: The Timbers and Thorns play here from late February to November, so soccer overlaps the Blazers' playoff push and fills the summer.

places.name: Chiles Center, University of Portland
places.why: Hosts the OSAA 6A state basketball finals in mid-March and the G League Rip City Remix from November to March, keeping local basketball going alongside the playoff push.

places.name: Spirit of 77
places.neighborhood: Lloyd District / Rose Quarter (NE MLK Jr. Blvd.)
places.why: A pregame and watch-party bar named after the 1977 title, and an obvious host for playoff nights and the June 5 anniversary.

people.name: Damian Lillard
people.role: Blazers guard returning from a torn Achilles; adidas signature athlete
people.why: His first games back at Moda Center are the emotional center of October. His Nike-made NBA jersey is likely the season's top gift item, though his personal marks belong to adidas.

people.name: Ja Morant
people.role: Blazers guard acquired from Memphis on June 29, 2026; Nike signature athlete
people.why: A new name for October jersey sales and a current Nike signature star in Nike's hometown backcourt. He needs brand-safety vetting before any hero launch.

people.name: Tom Dundon
people.role: Blazers owner since March 2026
people.why: His Moda Center lease talks and his trade-deadline appetite set the mood of the season. Fans watch him almost as closely as the roster.

people.name: Micah Nori
people.role: First-year Blazers head coach, hired from Minnesota's staff
people.why: His post-preseason call on whether Lillard or Morant comes off the bench is October's first big debate.

people.name: Bill Schonely
people.role: Blazers play-by-play voice from 1970 to 1998 (died 2023)
people.why: He coined "Rip City" in the franchise's first season, the name Portland still calls its fandom. Any use of his voice or likeness needs his estate.

people.name: Juneteenth Oregon
people.role: Portland's Juneteenth celebration, started in 1945 by Kaiser shipyard worker Clara Peoples
people.why: Albina's own summer moment, and in 2027 it falls on Father's Day weekend. Partner with organizers, credit and pay them, and don't brand it.

people.name: Portland Fire
people.role: WNBA team at Moda Center, inaugural season 2026
people.why: Carries Rip City from May to September. Nike makes every WNBA uniform, so the Fire are a summer bridge for Portland basketball product.

people.name: Portland Gear
people.role: Local Portland apparel brand founded by Marcus Harvey
people.why: Sets the local benchmark for speed and price on playoff and city tees, so it's a better collaborator than competitor.

moments.name: Home opener: Lillard back at Moda, Morant's debut
moments.why: October's hope peak, the biggest jersey-launch night, and the first chance to open a Blazermania 50 countdown.

moments.name: Pioneer Courthouse Square tree lighting
moments.why: Downtown's holiday kickoff falls on Black Friday and the Blazers' last Cup Friday, so the gifting window opens in one day.

moments.name: Christmas Ships Parade
moments.timing: December evenings on the Willamette and Columbia
moments.why: A tradition dating to 1954 that brings families to the riverbanks in cold, dark weather: a ready-made audience for warm layers.

moments.name: Playoff nights at Moda Center
moments.why: Giveaway shirts, rally towels and packed watch-party bars bring casual and lapsed fans back at once. It's the year's peak.

moments.name: Portland Rose Festival
moments.timing: Late May to mid-June; Grand Floral Parade on an early-June Saturday
moments.why: The Rose City's own festival fills downtown during the NBA Finals and the 1977 anniversary.

moments.name: 1977 championship 50th anniversary
moments.why: Turns a quiet June into a Portland peak and gives a season-long heritage story its finish line.

moments.name: Juneteenth Oregon
moments.timing: June 19, 2027 (Saturday, the eve of Father's Day)
moments.why: Northeast Portland's Juneteenth celebration dates to 1945. The community leads it, and brands follow.

moments.name: Waterfront Blues Festival
moments.why: Starts the dry season on the waterfront, when attention leaves the Blazers and goes outdoors.

vocabulary.meaning: Portland's name for itself and the Blazers' rallying cry, shouted by Bill Schonely in the team's first season.
Locals' name for the gray, rainy stretch from about November to February, the heart of the NBA season.
The warm, dry weeks of September (sometimes into October) after Labor Day, when Portland is outside and the Blazers are quiet.
A cool, gray June before the dry season starts, often around Rose Festival and draft time.
A short gap in the winter clouds. Portlanders stop what they're doing to stand in it.
The 1977 title run and the 814-game sellout streak that followed. Shorthand for peak Portland fandom.
What many locals still call Moda Center, its name from 1995 to 2013.
Lillard's late-game clutch persona. Fans say it all the time, but it's tied to his adidas line, so keep it in conversation and off Nike product.

designCues.cue: Rip City red, the playoff red-out color
designCues.source: The Blazers' primary red, worn by Moda Center crowds on playoff nights
designCues.use: The base for April rapid-response tees and rally gear. Keep it pure and saturated so a full arena reads as one color.

designCues.cue: Big Dark slate: the flat November-February cloud deck
designCues.source: Portland's winter sky from the Nov 1 clock change to February
designCues.use: Base for outerwear and lifestyle pieces, with red and white kept to stripe-width details.

designCues.cue: Sunbreak gold: the low, rare light of a winter sunbreak and Second Summer evenings
designCues.source: The Pacific Northwest sunbreak and September's dry golden light
designCues.use: A small accent for linings, zipper pulls and hangtags, and the lead color for the September back-to-school drop.

designCues.cue: '4:27 / 9:03' daylight bookends: Portland's earliest sunset (about 4:27 pm, early December) and latest, about 9:03 pm in late June
designCues.source: The 4.5-hour daylight swing that sets Portland's indoor and outdoor seasons
designCues.use: Sleeve hit or hangtag clock: 4:27 on the Big Dark pack and 9:03 on summer and June heritage pieces, so the two drops answer each other.

designCues.cue: '77 to '27 countdown: numbered monthly drops counting down from the home opener to June 5, 2027
designCues.source: The 50th anniversary of the June 5, 1977 title at Memorial Coliseum
designCues.use: Number each release (for example 8 of 9) and print the days remaining on hangtags, building to a June finale. Use team marks only under the NBA license, and 1977 likenesses only with the estates.

designCues.cue: MAX-ride shell: a seam-sealed, packable shell in Rip City red that stuffs into its own chest pocket and fits under a Moda Center seat
designCues.source: The November-to-March walk from Rose Quarter Transit Center to the arena in rain
designCues.use: The hero piece of the Nov 1 drop, with reflective hits for 5 pm darkness and a DWR finish.

productHooks: Big Dark Pack, dropping Nov 1, 2026 with the clock change: a slate DWR fleece hoodie and a packable Rip City red shell with a "4:27" sunset hangtag. Both are for weeknight fans riding MAX to the Rose Quarter.

Blazermania 50 countdown: numbered monthly heritage drops from the home opener to June 5, 2027. It ends in a Father's Day (June 20) capsule built with surviving 1977 players and the estates, pending team and league approval.
April rapid-response kit: Rip City red blanks and play-in and playoff graphics, pre-positioned with a Portland screen printer, ready to go on sale within 48 hours of a clinch.
Comeback-season gift bundle: Lillard and Morant Nike Swingman jerseys with youth sizes, marketed to the winter-break and ship-by deadline, not to a Christmas game Portland isn't playing.

Rip City summer: women's-first lightweight tees and sun hats in a shared Portland palette, sold May to September at Fire games, the Rose Festival and the Blues Festival. Each team's marks are licensed separately.
watchouts: Lillard is an adidas signature athlete. His Nike-made NBA jersey is fine, but "Dame Time", the wrist-tap and his personal marks stay off Nike product. Morant served suspensions in 2023 for displaying guns on social media, so vet any hero launch around him.

Nori may bring Lillard or Morant off the bench after the preseason, and Lillard is coming back from an Achilles tear. Don't sell a "starting backcourt" or a guaranteed comeback until the rotation is set.

The Moda Center lease is still being negotiated, and Dundon has said he won't pay for the renovation. Avoid multi-year launches tied to the arena, and check whether construction could displace summer events.
Weather sets the calendar. Outdoor events need rain plans from October to May, and heat and wildfire-smoke plans from July to September (the 2021 heat dome, recurring late-summer smoke).

Juneteenth Oregon and other Albina-rooted moments are community-led. Partner with them, credit and pay them, and don't brand them. The 1977 likenesses (Walton, Lucas, Ramsay, Schonely) need estates. Rose Festival, Fire, Timbers and Thorns marks need their own licenses.

uniform.headline: Five stripes a side: Glickman's 1970 pinwheel still carries Portland's look.
uniform.summary: The Blazers run one of the league's most disciplined identities: red, black and white, under a pinwheel of two sets of five stripes that has been redrawn but never replaced. Fans dress by era, from Walton's 1977 whites to Lillard's red "Rip City". City Editions keep circling plaid and carpet, and this season brings none at all. The untold material is the Coliseum, lower Albina, Vanport and Portland's double design birthright: the pinwheel in 1970 and the Swoosh in 1971.

insights.title: A heritage gap in a heritage year
insights.detail: Portland is re-wearing its 2019-20 City Edition in 2026-27 and wasn't among the eight franchises in Nike's Specter program. Yet this is the 50th-anniversary season of the 1976-77 title, clinched June 5, 1977 at Memorial Coliseum.
insights.implication: Lead the season with a '77-at-50 capsule: a warmup, a shooting shirt and a patch, plus a Classic Edition proposal if the team and league agree. The anniversary needs product before the playoffs.

insights.title: The pinwheel is a stripe system
insights.detail: Glickman's 1970 mark is two interlocking sets of five stripes, one for each team of five on the floor. Fans simply call it "the pinwheel". Redraws in the early 1990s, 2002 and 2017 changed the angle and the trim but kept the five-and-five logic.
insights.implication: Build trims, taping and knit patterns from five-plus-five stripes instead of adding new marks. It reads as Blazers from across a room, even without a logo.

insights.title: Fans dress by era, and the diagonal is the one they miss
insights.detail: Lifers wear 1977 Walton and Lucas, the Drexler, Porter and Kersey teams with the shoulder-to-hip red-and-black slash, Roy's #7 black "Portland", and Lillard's #0 red "Rip City". Mitchell & Ness largely owns vintage replicas.
insights.implication: Nike's lane is new-cut product that revives the diagonal slash, such as warmups, shooting shirts and a modern Statement or Classic treatment. Don't compete on straight replicas.

insights.title: Plaid and carpet are tapped out
insights.detail: Four straight City Editions have run on two motifs. The PDX carpet came in 2022-23. Dr. Jack plaid, honoring Jack Ramsay's loud sport coats, followed in 2023-24, then an all-over plaid in 2024-25 and a return to the carpet in 2025-26.
insights.implication: Open a fresh vein with the next new City Edition: Coliseum glass, Albina, radio-era "Rip City" or the 1970-71 design origin story. Keep plaid and carpet as linings and accents only.

insights.title: Two homecomings, two brands
insights.detail: Lillard returns from his Achilles tear for his first Blazers home games since 2023. Morant, a Nike signature athlete, debuts in Portland. Lillard is a longtime adidas signature athlete.
insights.implication: Stock deep in Lillard and Morant Swingmans across Association, Icon, Statement and the re-worn City Edition for the home opener and the Oct 30 Cup night against Golden State. Tell the player-exclusive story through Morant's Ja line.

insights.title: 'Rip City' is a radio call, not a slogan
insights.detail: Broadcaster Bill Schonely shouted "Rip City! All right!" after a Jim Barnett long jumper against the Lakers in the 1970-71 season. The phrase now sits on jerseys and courts. His voice, his other calls and the transistor-radio era that spread them have never been the design.
insights.implication: A broadcast-era treatment of "Rip City!" (call-sign lettering, the exclamation mark, a dial graphic) gives the mark a fresh, Portland-only story without inventing anything new.

places.name: Veterans Memorial Coliseum
places.why: The SOM glass-box arena (1960) where the Blazers played from 1970 to 1995, won the 1977 title and began the 814-game sellout streak. It was built on land cleared of Black homes and businesses.

places.name: Moda Center
places.why: The home since 1995, still called "the Rose Garden" by many fans. A publicly funded renovation is about to start and will reset the in-arena brand canvas.

places.name: Portland International Airport (PDX)
places.why: Source of the teal 1987 carpet that carried two City Editions. Its new mass-timber terminal is the city's newest civic design statement.

places.name: Nike Community Store
places.neighborhood: King, NE Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd
places.why: Nike's long-running Albina store is the most credible place to launch Portland product with the Northeast community instead of downtown tourists.

places.name: Deadstock Coffee
places.why: A sneaker-culture coffee shop founded by former Nike employee Ian Williams, where Portland's sneaker crowd gathers and drops get talked about. It closed its Old Town storefront in December 2025 and now operates from the lobby café of The Hoxton hotel.

places.name: Matt Dishman Community Center
places.why: A historic gym in the heart of Black Albina, and the natural partner venue for any Albina-rooted uniform or court story.

places.name: Irving Park courts
places.why: Northeast Portland's best-known outdoor pickup run, where local players will judge what Blazers gear actually looks good on a court.

places.name: Oregon Historical Society
places.why: The archive for Vanport, Albina, Coliseum and early-Blazers photography, and the place to research any heritage graphic before using it.

places.name: Vanport site (Delta Park / Portland International Raceway)
places.why: The site of the wartime city erased by the May 30, 1948 flood. Its displaced Black residents reshaped Albina.

people.name: Frank Glickman
people.role: Boston graphic artist and cousin of founder Harry Glickman; designed the 1970 pinwheel logo
people.why: The author of the franchise's one enduring mark. Crediting him by name gives heritage product an origin story beyond "retro".

people.name: Bill Schonely
people.role: Original Blazers broadcaster, 'the Schonz' (died 2023)
people.why: He coined "Rip City" in the team's first season, so every Rip City wordmark is his call.

people.name: Bill Walton
people.role: 1977 Finals MVP and Hall of Famer (died 2024)
people.why: The face of the title's 50th anniversary. His Deadhead tie-dye persona is beloved, but the Grateful Dead marks belong to someone else.

people.name: Clyde Drexler
people.role: Hall of Fame guard, 1983-1995 Blazer
people.why: "Clyde the Glide" in the diagonal-stripe uniform of the 1990 and 1992 Finals is the era Portland's forty- and fifty-something fans dress in.

people.name: Damian Lillard
people.role: All-time franchise scoring leader, back from an Achilles tear
people.why: His #0 is the most-worn modern Blazers jersey, and his return is the season's emotional jersey moment. His own marks run through adidas.

people.name: Carolyn Davidson
people.role: Designer of the Nike Swoosh (1971), then a Portland State University design student
people.why: With Glickman's pinwheel a year earlier, she makes Portland the birthplace of two of sport's best-known marks. Only this city has that design story.

people.name: Albina Vision Trust
people.role: Black-led nonprofit planning to rebuild lower Albina around the Rose Quarter
people.why: The rightful co-author of any Coliseum or Albina uniform story, since its work is on the same land the arenas sit on.

people.name: Portland Gear (Marcus Harvey)
people.role: Portland-pride apparel brand
people.why: Proof that a plain "Portland" wordmark sells. It shows the local appetite for city-first, not logo-first, product.

designCues.cue: Pinwheel red, used exactly to the NBA spec as the signal color on black or white grounds.
designCues.source: Official Blazers red, used since 1970 on the pinwheel and the 'Rip City' alternate.
designCues.use: Use it as the hit (stripes, numbers, a single zip or hood lining), not a full red base, so it stays a signal.

designCues.cue: True black base, the color of the Roy- and Lillard-era 'Portland' road and Icon jerseys.
designCues.source: Official Blazers black, the base of the Icon jersey and most fan outerwear.
designCues.use: Use as the ground for outerwear and lifestyle pieces, with red and white kept to stripe-width details.

designCues.cue: Five-and-five: two interlocking sets of five stripes, one per team of five, taken from the pinwheel and used as a trim system.
designCues.source: Frank Glickman's 1970 logo and its later redraws.
designCues.use: Use as five-stripe side taping, collar ribs, waistband jacquard or a knit hat cuff. Never stretch it to more or fewer than five.

designCues.cue: The diagonal slash: a shoulder-to-hip red-and-black stripe band across the chest.
designCues.source: The Blazers' home and road jerseys of the late 1970s to early 2000s, including the 1990 and 1992 Finals teams.
designCues.use: Use on warmups, shooting shirts and a modern Classic or Statement treatment for fans who dress in the Drexler era.

designCues.cue: Coliseum curtain wall: the tall glass-and-mullion grid around Memorial Coliseum's bowl, which glows at night.
designCues.source: Veterans Memorial Coliseum (Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, 1960), home of the 1977 title and the 814 sellouts.
designCues.use: Use as a woven jacquard or sublimated side panel, only within a story co-authored with Albina partners that acknowledges whose homes were cleared for the building.

designCues.cue: Broadcast-era 'Rip City!': call-sign lettering with the exclamation mark kept, plus a radio-dial graphic.
designCues.source: Schonely's 1971 call and the radio broadcasts that built Blazermania.
designCues.use: Use on a pregame tee, a jock tag reading "All right!" or a shooting-shirt back. These are team marks, so no outside license is needed.

designCues.cue: Waffle grid: the Bowerman waffle-sole pattern as a texture.
designCues.source: Nike's own Oregon origin story from the same years as the pinwheel and 'Rip City'.
designCues.use: Use as a debossed waistband, embossed jock tag or knit texture. It ties Nike to the Blazers' founding years without putting a Swoosh on the chest.

productHooks: '77 at 50 capsule: a Walton-era white warmup, a shooting shirt with a 1977-2027 patch and a proposed 1976-77 Classic Edition if the team and league agree. Release it at the home opener, with a second drop on June 5, 2027.

Homecoming and debut jerseys: deep Lillard #0 and Morant Swingman stock in all four editions, including the re-worn 2019-20 City, for the home opener and the Oct 30 Cup night. Add a Blazers player exclusive of Morant's Ja shoe.
Diagonal collection: a full-zip warmup, shooting shirt and mesh short with the shoulder-to-hip slash and five-and-five taping. Aim it at the Drexler-era fan and release it before a Lakers home date.

Next new City Edition brief, "Lower Albina": the Coliseum curtain-wall grid and Albina's history, co-designed and paid through Albina Vision Trust and Black Portland artists. Proceeds are committed to the neighborhood, and the launch is at the Nike Community Store on MLK.
"Two Marks" design-history tee and hoodie: Glickman's 1970 pinwheel and Davidson's 1971 Swoosh told as Portland's design birthright, with proceeds to a Portland State design scholarship.
watchouts: Third-party IP needs clearance or avoidance. That covers the PDX carpet (Port of Portland), Pendleton-style plaid, Grateful Dead imagery around Walton and Taco Bell's "Cha-lu-pa!" chant. It also covers Lillard's personal marks, "Dame Time" and "Dame D.O.L.L.A.", since he is an adidas athlete.

The "Trail Blazers" name evokes Oregon Trail settlers. Skip wagon and pioneer nostalgia and never use Native imagery. Route any Indigenous theme through Portland Native partners such as NAYA, credited and paid, with no sacred or ceremonial designs.

Coliseum and Rose Quarter nostalgia sits on land cleared of Black Albina homes and businesses. Any arena-heritage product has to carry that truth, co-authored with Albina partners and not as a February one-off.
Morant's 2023 NBA suspensions over firearm videos mean his debut product should be basketball-first, with no weapon-adjacent or "outlaw" framing. Launch roster-wide, not around one player.
Don't glamorize the early-2000s "Jail Blazers" era, and don't ship a fifth plaid or carpet story. Locals will read it as recycled.

untoldStories.story: Lower Albina and the Coliseum: the Black neighborhood cleared for Memorial Coliseum and I-5 in the 1950s and 60s, now the focus of Albina Vision Trust's plan to rebuild.
untoldStories.why: It's literally the ground the franchise was born on. Telling it with Albina partners, during a public-money arena renovation, would make the most meaningful uniform in team history.

untoldStories.story: Vanport, 1942-1948: Oregon's wartime boomtown, erased by the May 30, 1948 flood, whose displaced Black families were pushed into Albina by redlining.
untoldStories.why: Few Portlanders outside North and Northeast know it. Told with the Vanport Mosaic community, it explains how Black Portland and its basketball culture formed.

untoldStories.story: Rip City as a voice: Schonely's 1971 call and the transistor-radio Blazermania that spread it.
untoldStories.why: Every fan uses the phrase, but few know its sound and origin. A broadcast-era treatment honors the Schonz without inventing a new slogan.

untoldStories.story: Two marks, one city: Glickman's pinwheel in 1970 and PSU student Carolyn Davidson's Swoosh in 1971.
untoldStories.why: Only Portland can claim both. It frames the Nike-Blazers relationship as shared civic design history, not a sponsorship.
